Accountable obligation owner.value: Appointed Actuary owns the booked Part C unpaid claim liability for every H-contract/PBP; Reserving Actuary performs, Chief Actuary approves the assumption set before the Controller posts it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.254(a) (bid must be actuarially sound), 422.101(a),(b) (obligation to cover all Part A/B basic benefits, which drives the claim liability) and 422.2266(b) (low-performing-icon disclosure where the contract scores 2.5 stars or below for three years, which drives the Star bonus revenue assumption) re-read on eCFR at each quarter-end, together with the current NAIC Health Annual Statement Instructions for Underwriting & Investment Exhibit Part 2A/2B and Exhibit 6

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and year-end valuation of Medicare Advantage Part C liabilities: IBNR and reported-not-paid claim reserve by H-contract/PBP, provider capitation settlement and withhold accruals, CMS risk-adjustment receivable/payable, Star Ratings quality-bonus revenue accrual, MLR rebate liability and the premium deficiency reserve test against bid revenue

In-scope systems.value: Paid-claim lag triangles sourced from the Claims Platform, completion factors and PMPM projection run in the reserving platform, member months reconciled to the CMS MARx Monthly Membership Report, booked entries posted to the general ledger

Compliance procedure documented.value: MA Part C Reserve Valuation Procedure — data freeze and MMR reconciliation, lag-triangle build, completion-factor selection, incomplete-month PMPM projection, provider settlement accrual, risk-score true-up, margin for adverse deviation, PDR test, journal handoff and roll-forward

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Controller at the Reserve Committee; re-approved annually and on any CMS change to the HCC risk model version, the Star Ratings cut points or the 42 CFR 422.2266(b) low-performing status of a contract

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly Health statement reserve exhibits due 45 days after quarter end (May 15, Aug 15, Nov 15); annual statement Exhibit 6 and Part 2B due March 1; reserve support for the Part C bid due to Pricing two weeks before the first Monday in June bid submission

Deadline reminders configured.value: Valuation calendar entries fire at WD-5 (claims and enrollment data cut), WD-3 (model run complete), WD-2 (Reserve Committee approval) and WD-1 (GL journal cut-off) for each of the four valuation cycles

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Triangles, completion-factor exhibits, model output, assumption memo, roll-forward and sign-offs retained 10 years from the valuation date per the CMS MA record-retention requirement at 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any manual reserve override outside the approved procedure, any segment whose prior-period development exceeds 5% of the booked liability, and any late data cut are logged with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off every override, every restated segment and every remediation of a development breach before the next quarter's close

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every Part C reserve segment carried at the quarter-end valuation — each H-contract/PBP by benefit category (inpatient, outpatient, professional, ancillary, capitated) — plus the risk-adjustment, quality-bonus and MLR rebate accruals

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Reserve roll-forward, completion-factor and hindsight exhibits, MMR-to-model member-month tie-out and the Exhibit 6 reconciliation, producible for a CMS program audit or a state DOI financial examination within 5 business days of request

checklist.step: Freeze the valuation data cut and reconcile membership to the CMS MMR
actions: At WD-5 run the valuation extract job in the warehouse for paid claims through the cut date and member months by H-contract, PBP, county and month.
Download the CMS Monthly Membership Report (MMR) and Monthly Membership Detail files from MARx for each month in the experience period and load them next to the extract.
Compare member months per contract/PBP/month between the extract and the MMR; investigate any month differing by more than 0.5% with Enrollment Operations before the model runs.
Lock the extract as a dated, read-only snapshot named PARTC-VAL-<yyyy-qq>-<cutdate> and record the row counts and control totals on the valuation control sheet.
checklist.done: the dated snapshot is locked, member months tie to the MARx MMR within 0.5% per contract-month, and all differences are explained in writing.

checklist.step: Reconcile paid claims in the extract to the claims system and the general ledger
actions: Run the paid-claims control report in the Claims Platform for the same cut date, totalled by incurred month and benefit category.
Pull the medical claims expense and claims-paid clearing account balances for the period from the general ledger with the Controller's team.
Build a three-way tie: claims system paid, warehouse extract paid, GL cash paid; explain each reconciling item (voids, refunds, capitation, pharmacy carve-out, Part D exclusion).
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the valuation control sheet; no model run starts on an unreconciled extract.
checklist.done: claims system, warehouse extract and GL agree with every reconciling item named and quantified, and the reconciliation is signed.

checklist.step: Build paid-claim lag triangles by segment
actions: Load the locked extract into the reserving platform and build incurred-month by paid-month triangles for at least 36 incurred months.
Segment the triangles by H-contract and benefit category (inpatient facility, outpatient facility, professional, ancillary/DME, capitated) so fee-for-service and capitated cost do not blend.
Convert each triangle to PMPM using the reconciled member months from step 1 rather than the enrollment file used for billing.
Flag and annotate distortions on the triangle face: claim system conversions, provider contract terminations, benefit changes effective January 1, and any CMS payment-suspension months.
Export the triangle set into the valuation workpaper pack.
checklist.done: a 36-month PMPM triangle exists per contract and benefit category, built on reconciled member months, with distortions annotated.

checklist.step: Select and support the completion factors
actions: Compute age-to-age paid development factors and derive cumulative completion factors for lag 0 through lag 24 for each segment.
Select each factor from the 12-month volume-weighted average, the 6-month average and the prior-quarter selection, and write the reason for the pick in the selection column.
Where the selection sits outside the documented corridor (plus or minus 2 percentage points from the 12-month average), obtain the Chief Actuary's written approval before it is used.
Test the selected factors against the prior quarter's actual run-out and record the fit statistic on the exhibit.
checklist.done: every segment has a documented completion factor with a stated basis, a run-out fit statistic, and Chief Actuary approval on any out-of-corridor pick.

checklist.step: Project the incomplete recent months on a PMPM basis
actions: For the three most recent incurred months, replace the completion-factor estimate with a projected PMPM seeded from the trailing 12 completed months.
Apply the annual cost trend and the seasonality index agreed with Pricing, and adjust for the January 1 benefit and cost-share changes filed in the bid.
Adjust for known utilisation drivers: flu and respiratory season, an unusually long January enrollment surge, and any newly delegated or terminated provider group.
Blend the completion-factor and projection estimates with the documented credibility weights by lag month and show the blend on the exhibit.
checklist.done: the three most recent incurred months are estimated on a trended PMPM basis with documented credibility weights, not on raw completion factors.

checklist.step: Accrue provider capitation settlements, withholds and shared-savings balances
actions: Get from Provider Contracting the list of capitated and risk-sharing arrangements in force during the period, with the settlement formula and settlement date for each.
For each arrangement compute the surplus or deficit to date using the reconciled claims and capitation payments, and accrue the payable or the recoverable.
Accrue unreleased quality withholds and gainshare owed to delegated groups, and disclose any recoverable from a group whose financial solvency is in question.
Record each arrangement's accrual on its own line so the reserve exhibit does not mix fee-for-service IBNR with settlement balances.
checklist.done: every capitated or risk-sharing arrangement in force carries a computed settlement accrual on its own exhibit line with the formula referenced.

checklist.step: Accrue the CMS risk-adjustment receivable or payable
actions: Pull the latest Model Output Report (MOR) and MMR risk scores from MARx for each payment year still open (initial, mid-year and final reconciliation runs).
Estimate the incremental risk score from diagnoses submitted through EDPS but not yet reflected in a CMS sweep, using the historical accepted-encounter yield.
Multiply the incremental score by the contract's standardised bid and member months to compute the receivable, and haircut it for expected RADV/audit recoupment and deleted diagnoses.
Book the accrual by payment year and document the sweep dates relied on so the following quarter's true-up is traceable.
checklist.done: the risk-adjustment accrual is computed per payment year from named MOR/MMR sweeps, is net of an audit-recoupment haircut, and ties to the prior quarter's balance plus movement.

checklist.step: Compute the Part C MLR rebate liability
actions: Build the MLR numerator and denominator per contract on the CMS Part C MLR reporting definitions: incurred claims including the IBNR just computed, quality improving activity expenditures, and revenue net of taxes and fees.
Compute the ratio against the 85% minimum and calculate the remittance owed to CMS where the contract falls short.
Cross-check the credibility adjustment and the member-month basis against the prior year's filed MLR report before booking.
Book the liability by contract and hand the calculation to the Controller with the supporting numerator/denominator detail.
checklist.done: each contract has a computed MLR ratio against the 85% minimum and a booked remittance liability where it falls short, reconciled to the prior filed report.

checklist.step: Set the margin for adverse deviation and document the basis
actions: Measure the historical volatility of the estimate by segment using at least eight quarters of hindsight results.
Set the margin as a stated percentage of the best estimate per segment, higher for low-volume PBPs and newly entered counties where the triangle is thin.
Write the rationale into the assumption memo with reference to ASOP 5 (health claim liabilities) and ASOP 43 (unpaid claim estimates).
Show the best estimate, the margin and the booked figure as three separate columns on the reserve exhibit so the margin is never hidden inside the estimate.
checklist.done: each segment shows best estimate, stated margin and booked reserve separately, with the margin rationale written into the assumption memo.

checklist.step: Run the premium deficiency reserve test against bid revenue
actions: Group contracts as they are managed for the test and project remaining contract-year revenue from the CMS capitation rate, the risk score, the Part C rebate and the Star Ratings quality bonus.
Where a contract carries the low-performing icon under 42 CFR 422.2266(b), remove the quality-bonus revenue assumption and reflect the enrollment attrition that follows the icon disclosure.
Project remaining claims, administrative cost and the MLR remittance for the same period and compute the deficiency, if any.
Book a PDR for every deficient group and record the test, including the groups that passed, in the workpaper.
checklist.done: the PDR test covers every contract group, excludes quality-bonus revenue for low-performing contracts, and a reserve is booked wherever a deficiency is shown.

checklist.step: Roll forward the prior liability and measure prior-period development
actions: Build the roll-forward: opening liability, plus current-period incurred, less payments on prior periods, equals expected closing liability.
Compare the actual run-out of the prior quarter's liability to what was booked and compute favourable or adverse development in dollars and as a percentage.
Attribute each segment's development to a cause: completion factor, trend, seasonality, one-off large claims, or provider settlement.
Flag any segment beyond plus or minus 5% for the exception log and carry the cause into the next quarter's assumption review.
checklist.done: the roll-forward balances, development is quantified and attributed by segment, and every segment beyond 5% is logged.

checklist.step: Obtain independent peer review of the model run
actions: Confirm the model version used is the approved production version in the model inventory and that no uncontrolled change was made since the last validation.
Re-run two material segments independently from the locked extract and compare to the production result within a 1% tolerance.
Review the assumption memo against the prior quarter and challenge every changed assumption in writing on the review form.
Record the review outcome, the tolerance achieved and any conditions in the model governance repository against the valuation date.
checklist.done: an independent reviewer has re-run material segments within tolerance and logged a written challenge of every assumption change.

checklist.step: Present the reserve to the Reserve Committee for approval
actions: Circulate the reserve pack — exhibit by contract, roll-forward, development attribution, margin, PDR result and open exceptions — 48 hours before the committee.
Walk the committee through the movement from prior quarter and the reason for each material change in assumption.
Record the committee's decision, any directed adjustment, and the attendees in the minutes.
Release the approved figure to the Controller only after the minutes record the approval.
checklist.done: minuted committee approval of the booked figure exists and the released number matches the approved exhibit line for line.

checklist.step: Tie the reserve to the statement exhibits and post the journal entry
actions: Post the reserve journal by legal entity and contract to the claims-payable and claims-expense accounts before the WD-1 GL cut-off.
Tie the posted balance to the Health annual statement Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2A/2B and Exhibit 6 lines, and to the quarterly statement equivalents.
Reconcile the ledger balance back to the actuarial exhibit total to the dollar and attach the tie-out to the close binder.
Escalate any difference to the Chief Actuary the same day rather than plugging it.
checklist.done: the GL balance equals the approved actuarial exhibit total and the statement exhibit tie-out is attached to the close binder.

checklist.step: Archive the valuation workpapers under the 10-year retention label
actions: Move the workpaper pack (locked extract control totals, triangles, completion-factor exhibits, PMPM projection, accrual calculations, PDR test, roll-forward, peer review, committee minutes, GL tie-out) into the evidence repository under REG-051-C01 and the valuation date.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d) and set the disposition hold so CMS audit periods cannot age out.
Confirm the pack is indexed and searchable by H-contract number, valuation date and benefit category.
checklist.done: the complete valuation pack is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by H-contract number and valuation date.

testing.step: Build the population of reserve segments carried at the valuation date
actions: Extract every reserve line booked at the quarter-end by H-contract, PBP, benefit category and accrual type (IBNR, settlement, risk adjustment, quality bonus, MLR rebate, PDR).
Reconcile the extract total to the general ledger claims-payable balance and to the statement Exhibit 6 line; any unreconciled dollar stops the test.
Confirm no contract active in MARx during the period is missing from the population by comparing the contract list to the MMR contract roster.
Sign the population as complete and record the control totals in the workpaper.
testing.done: the segment population reconciles to the GL and Exhibit 6, covers every MARx-active contract, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Re-reconcile the model inputs to the source systems independently
actions: Re-run the paid-claims total from the Claims Platform for the valuation cut date without using the actuarial extract.
Re-pull member months from the MARx MMR files for every month in the experience period and compare to the member months used in the PMPM denominators.
Quantify any difference by contract-month and confirm the valuation team's explanation covers it; unexplained differences above 0.5% are exceptions.
Attach both independent pulls to the workpaper as the reconciliation evidence.
testing.done: independently pulled claims and member months agree with the model inputs, or every difference above 0.5% is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of segments
actions: Take 100% of segments representing more than 5% of the total booked liability and 100% of segments with a booked PDR or a low-performing contract.
Draw 15 further segments at random using a recorded, reproducible seed from the remaining population.
Record the population size, the seed, the selection date and the coverage of the sample as a percentage of the booked liability.
Note that every segment flagged in the prior quarter's exception log is a mandatory retest row on top of the sample.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed, covers all material and PDR segments, and carries forward every prior-quarter exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the completion-factor selection for each sampled segment
actions: Rebuild the age-to-age development from the locked extract in the reserving platform without opening the valuation team's selection sheet.
Reach an independent completion factor per lag month, then compare to the booked selection and to the documented corridor.
Treat any selection outside the corridor with no Chief Actuary approval on file as a fail, not a documentation gap.
Capture the independent factor exhibit into the workpaper alongside the booked one.
testing.done: each sampled segment has an independently derived completion factor, a documented comparison, and an approval on file for every out-of-corridor pick.

testing.step: Recompute the IBNR for the sampled segments
actions: Apply the independent completion factors and an independently trended PMPM to the reconciled member months to produce a recomputed liability per sampled segment.
Compare the recomputed figure to the booked figure and express the difference in dollars and as a percentage of the segment.
Confirm the booked figure equals best estimate plus the stated margin, and that the margin percentage matches the assumption memo.
List any segment where the difference exceeds 5%, or where the margin cannot be identified separately, as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled segment has a recomputed liability, a quantified difference, and a margin that reconciles to the assumption memo.

testing.step: Test the risk-adjustment, quality-bonus and MLR accruals
actions: Trace the risk scores used in the accrual back to the named MOR and MMR sweep files downloaded from MARx and confirm the payment year is correctly assigned.
Recompute the receivable for two contracts as incremental score times standardised bid times member months, and check the RADV recoupment haircut is applied and supported.
Recompute the Part C MLR ratio for one contract from the numerator and denominator detail and confirm the remittance against the 85% minimum.
Confirm no quality-bonus revenue is accrued for any contract carrying the 42 CFR 422.2266(b) low-performing icon.
testing.done: risk-adjustment, quality-bonus and MLR accruals trace to named CMS files and recompute within tolerance, with no bonus revenue on low-performing contracts.

testing.step: Run the hindsight test on prior-period development
actions: Take the liability booked four quarters ago and measure the actual run-out paid against it through the current cut date.
Compute favourable or adverse development in aggregate and per segment, and compare against the plus or minus 3% aggregate and 5% segment thresholds.
Test whether the same segments breach in consecutive quarters, which indicates a biased assumption rather than volatility.
Record the hindsight exhibit and the threshold conclusion in the workpaper.
testing.done: development is measured against the stated thresholds, repeat breaches are identified, and the hindsight exhibit is in the workpaper.

testing.step: Verify governance, model control and approvals
actions: Confirm the model version run at the valuation date is the approved production version in the model inventory, with no change outside change control.
Confirm the Reserve Committee minutes record approval of the booked figure and that the released number matches the approved exhibit.
Confirm the peer reviewer did not build or run the sampled segments, and that the review form records a written challenge of each assumption change.
Confirm the workpaper pack carries the 10-year retention label under 42 CFR 422.504(d).
testing.done: model version, committee approval, reviewer independence and retention labelling are each evidenced or logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the contract, segment, dollar effect and the control that failed.

Assign a root cause from the standard list (data cut error, completion factor bias, trend seed stale, settlement formula misapplied, sweep file misassigned, unapproved override) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next valuation cycle and, where the exception changes a filed figure, notify the Appointed Actuary for restatement assessment the same day.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a named root cause, an owner, a remediation date inside the next cycle and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sampled segments and compare it to the 3% aggregate and 5% segment development thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the independent reviewer, who built and ran no sampled segment, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any restatement risk to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-051-C01.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the appointment, qualification and independence of the Appointed Actuary
actions: Pull the board resolution appointing the Appointed Actuary for the reporting year and confirm it names the individual, the entity and the effective date.
Collect the actuary's current qualification statement showing the basic and continuing education required to sign a health opinion, plus Academy membership.
Where the appointment changed during the year, prepare the notice to the domiciliary commissioner within the period required by that state's adoption of NAIC Model 822 and file the sent copy.
Record the confirmation and attach the resolution and qualification statement to the opinion folder for the reporting year.
checklist.done: a current board resolution, a signed qualification statement and, where applicable, a filed change-of-actuary notice sit in the opinion folder.

checklist.step: Define the scope of the opinion and the items it will cover
actions: List the statement items the opinion will cover: unpaid claims and claim adjustment expense, premium deficiency reserve, aggregate health policy reserves, amounts receivable and payable under CMS risk-sharing arrangements.
Confirm with the Controller which lines of the Health annual statement each item maps to (Exhibit 6, Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2A/2B) and record the mapping.
State explicitly what is excluded — Part D reserves opined separately, and any run-off commercial block — so the scope paragraph is unambiguous.
Circulate the scope memo to the Chief Actuary and the CFO for agreement before drafting begins.
checklist.done: an agreed scope memo names every opined item, its statement line, and every exclusion.

checklist.step: Obtain ASOP 23 data reliance letters from every data provider
actions: Request a signed reliance letter from the Controller covering the financial data, from the claims data owner covering paid-claim and encounter data, and from Enrollment Operations covering MARx membership data.
Require each letter to state the extraction date, the systems used, the completeness and accuracy assertion and the signer's authority.
Perform and document the actuary's own reasonableness checks on the reliance data: period-over-period claim PMPM, member-month continuity and duplicate-claim rate.
Chase any letter outstanding at January 15 and escalate to the CFO the same week; no opinion is signed on unlettered data.
checklist.done: a signed, dated reliance letter exists for each data source, with the actuary's own reasonableness checks documented alongside.

checklist.step: Reconcile the opined reserve figures to the annual statement pages
actions: Open the draft Health annual statement blank and read the reserve figures on Exhibit 6, Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2A/2B and the liabilities page.
Tie each figure to the approved actuarial exhibit produced at the December 31 valuation, dollar for dollar, by legal entity.
Investigate and clear any difference with the Controller before the opinion is drafted; a plug is never accepted.
Attach the signed tie-out schedule to the opinion folder.
checklist.done: every opined figure equals the corresponding annual statement line to the dollar and the tie-out is signed.

checklist.step: Perform and document reserve adequacy testing behind the opinion
actions: Run the year-end hindsight study on the prior year-end liability and quantify favourable or adverse development in aggregate and by contract.
Run a gross premium valuation for the coming contract year using the filed bid revenue, projected claims and administrative cost, and identify any deficient group.
Sensitivity-test the result for a 5% adverse claim trend, a risk-score reduction from the next CMS sweep and a RADV recoupment scenario.
Record each test, its result and its conclusion in the memorandum's adequacy section.
checklist.done: hindsight, gross premium valuation and named sensitivities are each run, documented, and concluded on in the memorandum.

checklist.step: Take in the compliance-program and UM-governance findings that bear on the reserves
actions: Extract from the GRC platform the year's monitoring and auditing findings raised under the 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi) compliance-program elements, filtered to those with a financial or claim-payment impact.
Add the utilization management committee's findings required under 42 CFR 422.137(d), including any determination that a UM policy caused improper denials now expected to be paid on appeal.
Add any open CMS corrective action plan, civil money penalty or enrollment sanction with a quantifiable liability.
Hand the Appointed Actuary a written schedule of these items with estimated dollar effect and status.
checklist.done: the actuary holds a written schedule of compliance, UM and CMS enforcement findings with estimated financial effect and status.

checklist.step: Draft the opinion using the prescribed opinion language
actions: Draft the identification, scope, reliance and opinion paragraphs following the NAIC Health Annual Statement Instructions wording, changing prescribed language only where a deviation is genuinely required.
Name each reliance in the reliance paragraph by person, role and subject matter, matching the letters collected earlier.
State the opinion type — unqualified, qualified, adverse or inconclusive — and where anything other than unqualified is proposed, escalate to the CFO and Audit Committee before circulation.
Add a relevant comment paragraph for the CMS-specific risks: risk-score recoupment exposure, the MLR remittance and any low-performing contract.
checklist.done: a draft opinion exists in prescribed form with named reliances, a stated opinion type and CMS-specific relevant comments.

checklist.step: Write the supporting actuarial memorandum
actions: Write the memorandum sections required by ASOP 22 and the statement instructions: purpose and scope, description of the business, data and reliance, methods and assumptions, changes from the prior year, adequacy testing and conclusion.
Include the completion-factor and margin exhibits, the roll-forward and the PDR test result so a reviewing actuary can re-perform the work.
Document every assumption change from the prior year with the reason and the dollar effect.
File the memorandum in the document repository with restricted access and a link to the opinion folder.
checklist.done: a memorandum with every ASOP 22 required section, re-performable exhibits and a quantified list of assumption changes is filed.

checklist.step: Obtain independent peer review of the opinion and memorandum
actions: Assign a reviewing actuary who did not produce the valuation and give them the memorandum, exhibits and reliance letters.
Require the reviewer to test the arithmetic of the reserve exhibit, challenge the margin and completion factor selections, and confirm the prescribed opinion wording has not been silently altered.
Log every review comment and the disposition of each on a review form; unresolved comments block signature.
Sign the review form and place it in the opinion folder.
checklist.done: a signed peer review form with every comment dispositioned sits in the opinion folder before signature.

checklist.step: Have Regulatory Counsel clear the wording and any qualification
actions: Read the draft opinion against the state's actuarial opinion regulation and the statement instructions for prohibited deviations from prescribed language.
Assess any qualification or relevant comment for the disclosure it triggers with the domiciliary commissioner and with CMS.
Confirm the reliance paragraph does not disclaim responsibility the actuary cannot lawfully disclaim.
Record clearance, or required changes, in writing on the opinion folder.
checklist.done: counsel has recorded written clearance of the opinion wording, including any qualification and its disclosure consequences.

checklist.step: Report the opinion to the Audit Committee and the board
actions: Table the draft opinion, the adequacy conclusion, the assumption changes and any qualification at the February Audit Committee meeting.
Present the compliance-program and UM findings schedule so the board sees the operational drivers behind the reserve.
Record the committee's acknowledgement, questions and any directed action in the minutes.
Post the pack to the board portal with the retention and access controls applied.
checklist.done: the minutes record the committee's acknowledgement of the opinion, the adequacy conclusion and any qualification.

checklist.step: Sign and date the opinion
actions: Confirm the reserve figures in the final blank still equal the opined figures after all closing entries; re-tie if the blank moved.
Sign the opinion, print the actuary's name, title, credential and the date, and state the entity and NAIC company code.
Produce the signed PDF with the signature page embedded and no editable fields.
Hand the signed PDF to Regulatory Reporting for inclusion in the March 1 annual statement filing.
checklist.done: a signed, dated opinion PDF naming entity and NAIC code, tied to the final blank, is with Regulatory Reporting.

checklist.step: Prepare the memorandum for delivery on regulator request
actions: Package the memorandum, exhibits and reliance letters as a single delivery pack ready to go out within 30 days of any commissioner request.
Record in the opinion folder which state requested it, on what date and by what channel, and diarise the 30-day due date.
Send via the state's secure filing channel and retain the transmission receipt.
Notify the Appointed Actuary and Regulatory Counsel of every request the day it arrives.
checklist.done: the delivery pack is standing ready and every request has a diarised 30-day due date with a retained transmission receipt.

checklist.step: Handle any post-signature change to the reserves
actions: Where a closing entry, audit adjustment or restatement changes an opined figure after signature, stop and assess whether the signed opinion remains supportable.
Where it does not, draft an amended opinion, obtain counsel clearance and notify the domiciliary commissioner and the Audit Committee.
Log the event in the issue tracker with the dollar effect, cause and the date the amended opinion was filed.
Feed the cause into next year's close calendar so the same timing gap does not recur.
checklist.done: any post-signature reserve change has a documented supportability assessment and, where needed, a filed amended opinion and regulator notification.

checklist.step: Archive the opinion pack under the 10-year retention label
actions: File the signed opinion, memorandum, reliance letters, peer review form, counsel clearance, board minute reference and statement tie-out under REG-051-C02 and the reporting year.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d) and set a legal hold flag usable if a CMS audit opens.
Confirm the pack is searchable by legal entity, NAIC company code and reporting year.
checklist.done: the complete opinion pack is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by entity and reporting year.

testing.step: Build the population of opinions required for the reporting year
actions: List every legal entity writing Medicare Advantage in the year from the licence register and the MARx contract roster.
Match each entity to the annual statement filed for it and identify which required a Statement of Actuarial Opinion.
Reconcile the entity list to the CMS contract-to-entity mapping so no H-contract sits in an entity that filed no opinion.
Sign the population as complete and record it in the workpaper.
testing.done: the entity population reconciles to both the licence register and the MARx contract roster and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Confirm every population entity has a signed opinion in the filed statement
actions: Open the filed annual statement for each entity and locate the actuarial opinion attachment as filed, not the working draft.
Confirm the signature, printed name, credential, title, date, entity name and NAIC company code are all present.
Confirm the signature date is on or before the March 1 filing date; a later date is an automatic fail.
Capture each filed opinion PDF into the workpaper.
testing.done: every entity has a filed, signed and dated opinion captured in the workpaper, signed on or before March 1.

testing.step: Verify appointment and qualification of each signer
actions: Trace each signer to a board resolution appointing them for that entity and that reporting year.
Read the signer's qualification statement and confirm the basic and continuing education claimed covers health reserve opinions.

Where the appointment changed in the year, confirm the change-of-actuary notice to the domiciliary commissioner was sent within the period required by that state's Model 822 adoption, and inspect the transmission evidence.
Log any signer without a current resolution or qualification statement as a fail.
testing.done: every signer is traced to a board appointment and a current qualification statement, and any change of actuary has evidenced regulator notice.

testing.step: Re-tie the opined figures to the filed statement
actions: Read the reserve figures from the filed statement Exhibit 6 and Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2A/2B independently of the actuarial tie-out.
Compare each to the figure stated or referenced in the opinion and memorandum, entity by entity.
Any difference, however small, is an exception; note the direction and dollar amount.
Attach the independent tie-out to the workpaper.
testing.done: the opined figures equal the filed statement figures to the dollar for every entity, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test the ASOP 23 reliance chain
actions: For each reliance named in the opinion paragraph, locate the corresponding signed letter and confirm it covers the same subject matter and period.
Confirm each letter states the extraction date, systems used and a completeness and accuracy assertion, and is signed by someone with authority over that data.
Confirm the actuary's own reasonableness checks on the relied-upon data are documented, not merely asserted.
A reliance named with no letter, or a letter with no assertion, is a fail.
testing.done: every named reliance has a matching signed letter with an assertion, and the actuary's own checks are evidenced.

testing.step: Re-perform a slice of the adequacy testing behind the opinion
actions: Independently recompute the year-end hindsight development on the prior year-end liability from the locked claims extract.
Re-run the gross premium valuation for the two largest contracts using the filed bid revenue and compare the deficiency conclusion.
Re-run the 5% adverse trend and risk-score reduction sensitivities and compare the results to those stated in the memorandum.
Any conclusion that flips under re-performance is an exception escalated the same day.
testing.done: hindsight, gross premium valuation and the stated sensitivities re-perform to the same conclusions, or the difference is escalated.

testing.step: Verify the compliance-program and UM findings were considered
actions: Extract the year's findings under the 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi) elements and the 42 CFR 422.137(d) UM committee minutes independently of the actuarial folder.
Compare the extract to the schedule handed to the Appointed Actuary and identify any financially material finding omitted.
Trace at least two material findings into the memorandum to confirm they were considered in the reserve or explicitly ruled out.
An omitted material finding is an exception regardless of its dollar effect.
testing.done: the independently extracted findings are all reflected in the schedule given to the actuary, and material items are traced into the memorandum.

testing.step: Test peer review, counsel clearance and board reporting
actions: Confirm the peer reviewer produced no part of the valuation and that the review form shows a disposition against every comment.
Confirm Regulatory Counsel recorded written clearance of the wording, and specifically of any qualification or relevant comment.
Read the Audit Committee minutes and confirm the opinion, the adequacy conclusion and any qualification were tabled before signature.
Missing clearance or reporting after signature is an exception.
testing.done: peer review independence, written counsel clearance and pre-signature board reporting are each evidenced or logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, the opinion element that failed and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause (appointment lapse, reliance letter not chased, close timing, prescribed wording altered, findings schedule incomplete) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next December 1 appointment checkpoint so the fix lands before next year's cycle.
Where the exception affects a filed opinion, open an amended-opinion assessment with the Appointed Actuary and Regulatory Counsel the same day.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, a remediation date before the next cycle and, where filed work is affected, an amendment assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against the zero-tolerance threshold for unsigned, unqualified-signer or untied opinions.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the actuarial function and had no role in the opinion, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any amended-opinion risk to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
File the workpaper under REG-051-C02 with the reporting year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Build the entity-by-jurisdiction filing matrix for the reporting year
actions: Pull the current certificate of authority list for each MA legal entity from the licence register, including states entered or exited during the year.

For each state read the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions filing checklist column to see whether it takes the statement through the NAIC only, direct, or both, and whether it demands a hard copy or a jurat page.
Record for each entity-jurisdiction pair: filing method, due date, fee amount, fee channel (OPTins or state portal) and whether the actuarial opinion must be attached or filed separately.
Have the Controller approve the matrix by January 31; a state exited mid-year still files for the period it was licensed.
checklist.done: an approved matrix names every entity-jurisdiction pair with method, due date, fee and opinion handling, including part-year licences.

checklist.step: Assemble the annual statement blank for each entity
actions: Load the trial balance from the general ledger into the current-year Health blank and map every account to its statement line.

Complete the exhibits and schedules relevant to Medicare Advantage: Exhibit 6, Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Parts 1, 2A and 2B, the Analysis of Operations by Line of Business with the Medicare Title XVIII column, and the Five-Year Historical.
Complete the jurat page with the officers' names and titles and the NAIC company code.
Circulate the draft blank to the Controller and the Appointed Actuary for review before validation.
checklist.done: a complete draft blank exists per entity with the Medicare Title XVIII columns populated and the jurat page filled.

checklist.step: Attach the signed actuarial opinion to the correct statement section
actions: Take the signed opinion PDF handed over by the Appointed Actuary and check the entity name, NAIC company code and reporting year on its face.
Attach it to the annual statement in the actuarial opinion attachment slot for the entity, not as a general supplemental document.
Re-read the reserve figures cited in the opinion against the blank's Exhibit 6 and Part 2B lines and stop the filing on any difference.
Record the attachment and the tie-out in the filing checklist for the entity.
checklist.done: the signed opinion is attached in the correct slot for each entity and its figures tie to the blank being filed.

checklist.step: Run the NAIC validation edits and clear every error
actions: Run the current-year NAIC cross-checks and validation edits in the reporting tool for each entity.
Clear every fatal error and document a written explanation for each surviving warning, since states read the warning list.
Re-run validation after any correction and keep the final clean validation report with the filing pack.
Escalate an error that cannot be cleared to the Controller before submission, never suppress it.
checklist.done: a clean validation report exists per entity with a written explanation for every remaining warning.

checklist.step: Obtain officer review and sign-off on the statement
actions: Review the final blank, the analytical variance commentary against prior year and the opinion attachment.
Confirm the officers named on the jurat page are the officers who will sign and that their titles are current.
Sign or authorise the electronic signature on the jurat page and record the date.
Release the filing pack to Regulatory Reporting for transmission.
checklist.done: the jurat page carries current officer signatures and dates, and the pack is released for transmission.

checklist.step: Upload the statement to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company's filing credentials and open the Financial Data Repository annual statement upload.
Upload the annual statement file and the actuarial opinion attachment for each entity, selecting the correct year, statement type and company code.
Wait for the repository to return the processing result and confirm status is accepted rather than pending or rejected.
Save the confirmation page and the file receipt into the filing evidence folder named <entity>-AS-<year>-NAIC.
checklist.done: every entity shows an accepted NAIC upload with the opinion attached and the confirmation is saved.

checklist.step: File with the domiciliary state and every other required jurisdiction
actions: Work the matrix jurisdiction by jurisdiction, submitting through each state's required channel and applying any state-specific transmittal or cover letter.
Where a state demands the opinion filed separately or a wet-signature jurat mailed, complete that step and record the courier tracking number.
Tick each jurisdiction off the matrix only once a confirmation or receipt exists, never on the fact of sending.
Escalate any jurisdiction still open at T-1 business day to the Controller by name.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction on the matrix shows a confirmation or receipt, and none is ticked on send alone.

checklist.step: Pay the filing fees and capture the receipts
actions: Pay each state's annual statement filing fee through OPTins or the state's own portal, matching the amount on the matrix.
Where a state ties the filing to premium tax or an annual assessment, coordinate the payment date with the Tax Manager so the filing is not held up.
Capture the payment confirmation number and the receipt PDF against the matrix row.
Reconcile total fees paid to the accrued filing fee account in the general ledger.
checklist.done: every fee is paid with a captured receipt and the total reconciles to the accrued filing fee balance.

checklist.step: File the supplemental and separately-dated filings
actions: Work the NAIC checklist for the supplements due March 1 and April 1 for the Health blank and confirm which apply to the MA entities.
Diarise the audited financial statements due June 1 and the Management's Discussion and Analysis with their own owners.
Submit each supplement through the same NAIC and state channels and capture confirmations on the matrix.
Report supplement status to the Controller weekly through the filing season.
checklist.done: every applicable supplement is filed by its own due date with a captured confirmation and a weekly status report.

checklist.step: Report the CMS-facing financial information required of the MA organization
actions: Check the HPMS memoranda and the reporting requirements technical specifications for the financial and Part C reporting sections due for the contract year under 42 CFR 422.516.
Upload the required financial reports through the HPMS module for each H-contract by the date stated in the technical specifications.
Reconcile the figures reported to CMS to the same figures in the statutory statement and explain every definitional difference in a bridging note.
Save the HPMS submission confirmation with the statutory filing pack so the two views are evidenced together.
checklist.done: the CMS financial reports are submitted for every H-contract with a bridging note reconciling them to the statutory statement.

checklist.step: Work state deficiency notices within 30 days of receipt
actions: Log every deficiency, interrogatory or analyst question the day it arrives with the state, entity, date received and the 30-day due date.
Route reserve and opinion questions to the Appointed Actuary and financial statement questions to the Controller, with an internal due date at day 20.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any response that concedes a late or incomplete filing before it is sent.
Send through the state's own channel, capture the response and the acknowledgement, and close the tracker item only on acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every deficiency has a logged receipt date, a routed owner, a cleared response sent within 30 days and a captured acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Amend and refile where a filed figure changes
actions: Where an audit adjustment or restatement changes a filed figure, prepare an amended statement marked as an amendment with the reason stated.
Ask the Appointed Actuary whether the opinion remains supportable and obtain an amended opinion where it does not.
Refile to the NAIC repository and to every jurisdiction that received the original, not only the domiciliary state.
Log the amendment, its cause and its distribution list in the issue tracker.
checklist.done: every amended figure is refiled to every jurisdiction that had the original, with the opinion position resolved and logged.

checklist.step: Report filing completion to the CFO and the Audit Committee
actions: Produce the completion report: entity-jurisdiction pairs due, filed, confirmed, fees paid, deficiencies open and any late filing.
Present it to the CFO within five business days of March 1 and to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
Name every late or missed filing individually with the exposure and the remediation owner.
Record the committee's acknowledgement in the minutes.
checklist.done: a completion report naming every late or missed filing has been presented to the CFO and minuted at the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Update the filing calendar and matrix from the season's lessons
actions: Record every state whose requirement, fee or channel differed from the matrix and correct next year's matrix template.
Adjust the T-30/T-14/T-5 reminder points where a state's process took longer than the buffer allowed.
Add any newly entered state and remove any exited state, with the effective dates of each licence change.
Have the Controller re-approve the updated matrix.
checklist.done: the matrix and reminder schedule are corrected from the season's actual experience and re-approved by the Controller.

checklist.step: Archive the filing evidence under the 10-year retention label
actions: File the filed blanks, opinion attachments, validation reports, NAIC and state confirmations, fee receipts, HPMS confirmations and deficiency correspondence under REG-051-C03 and the reporting year.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm the pack is searchable by legal entity, NAIC company code, jurisdiction and reporting year.
checklist.done: the filing evidence pack is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by entity, jurisdiction and year.

testing.step: Rebuild the filing obligation population independently
actions: Rebuild the entity-jurisdiction list from the certificate of authority register rather than from the filing matrix.
Add any state entered or exited during the year using the licence effective dates, since part-year licences still file.
Compare the rebuilt list to the matrix used and treat any pair missing from the matrix as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete and record the count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the independently rebuilt population is reconciled to the filing matrix and every missing pair is logged.

testing.step: Confirm an accepted submission exists for every pair
actions: For each pair, open the retained NAIC iSite+ or state confirmation and read the status, the entity, the year and the submission timestamp.
Confirm the status is accepted, not pending or rejected, and that no later resubmission superseded it without explanation.
Where only an email of transmission exists with no confirmation, record it as unevidenced and treat it as an exception.
Capture each confirmation into the workpaper.
testing.done: every pair has a captured, accepted confirmation, and transmission-only evidence is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the filing timeliness against March 1
actions: Read the submission timestamp on each confirmation in the state's own time zone as stated on the receipt.
Compare it to the March 1 statutory deadline, or the state's stated alternative date, and compute days early or late.
Confirm supplemental filings met their own March 1 or April 1 dates and the audited financials met June 1.
Any filing after its deadline is a fail regardless of whether the state objected.
testing.done: every filing has a computed timeliness result against its own deadline and every late filing is recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Draw and document a sample for detailed inspection
actions: Take 100% of domiciliary filings and 100% of pairs where a deficiency was raised or a fee dispute arose.
Draw 12 further pairs at random from the remainder using a recorded seed.
Record the population size, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-year exception pair as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all domiciliary and deficiency pairs, and carries prior-year exceptions forward.

testing.step: Verify the signed opinion is inside each sampled filed statement
actions: Open the statement as filed for each sampled pair and locate the actuarial opinion in the actuarial opinion attachment slot.
Confirm the opinion is the signed version with entity name, NAIC company code, credential and date, not a draft.
Where the state requires the opinion filed separately, confirm that separate filing has its own confirmation.
A statement filed with no opinion attached is a reportable failure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled filing evidences the signed opinion in the required place, or the omission is reported.

testing.step: Re-tie the filed statement figures to the ledger and the actuarial exhibit
actions: Pull the year-end trial balance from the general ledger independently and map the claims-payable and premium accounts to the statement lines.
Compare to Exhibit 6, Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2A/2B and the Medicare Title XVIII column in the Analysis of Operations for the sampled entities.
Compare the same lines to the approved actuarial reserve exhibit at December 31.
Any difference between ledger, statement and actuarial exhibit is an exception with the dollar amount recorded.
testing.done: ledger, filed statement and actuarial exhibit agree for the sampled entities, or each difference is quantified and logged.

testing.step: Test fee payment and the validation record
actions: For each sampled pair, match the OPTins or state portal receipt to the fee amount recorded on the matrix.
Reconcile the total fees paid across the season to the general ledger filing fee account.
Read the retained NAIC validation report for each sampled entity and confirm no fatal error remained and each warning has a written explanation.
An unexplained warning or an unreconciled fee is an exception.
testing.done: sampled fees match the matrix and reconcile to the ledger, and each validation report is clean with explained warnings.

testing.step: Recompute deficiency response timeliness
actions: Extract every deficiency, interrogatory and analyst question logged for the year with its received date and response date.
Recompute elapsed days from receipt to the state's acknowledgement and compare against the 30-day requirement.
Confirm each response that conceded a late or incomplete filing carries Regulatory Counsel's clearance before it was sent.
Confirm no item is closed without a state acknowledgement on file.
testing.done: every deficiency shows a recomputed elapsed-day result within 30 days, counsel clearance where required, and an acknowledgement on file.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, jurisdiction, what was missed and the penalty or examination exposure.
Assign a root cause (matrix omission, licence change not picked up, close timing, channel change unnoticed, fee unpaid, deficiency unrouted) and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next January 31 matrix approval so the fix is in place for the next season.
Where a jurisdiction was missed entirely, open a voluntary-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel the same day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and a remediation date before the next matrix approval, with disclosure assessed where a filing was missed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over the entity-jurisdiction population against the zero-tolerance threshold for missed or late filings.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Regulatory Reporting and transmitted no filing, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-051-C03 with the reporting year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: AAT complete and peer-reviewed before the actuarial opinion is signed in late February; memorandum available to the domiciliary commissioner within 30 days of request; refreshed interim analysis whenever a service area expansion or a network termination changes projected cash flows materially

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every MA legal entity subject to asset adequacy analysis, each of its liability segments, the assets assigned to them, and every scenario in the tested set including the network-adequacy stress

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every scenario must end with positive surplus and no negative interim cash position; any scenario failing without a booked additional reserve is a fail, as is any assumption change not documented and peer-reviewed

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with interim refresh on material change; the test runs annually before the opinion signature and re-runs on demand whenever a service area or network change triggers an interim analysis

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual AAT verification workpaper (scope reconciliation, asset assignment test, scenario re-runs, network stress recomputation, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C04 and the reporting year

checklist.step: Define the AAT scope, segmentation and testing method
actions: List the legal entities in scope and, for each, the liability segments to be tested: Part C claim liabilities, provider settlement balances, MLR remittance and any long-duration supplemental benefit obligation.

Choose and record the method per segment — cash flow testing for the interest-sensitive and longer-duration items, gross premium valuation for the short-duration claim liabilities — with the ASOP 22 rationale.
Agree the scope memo with the Appointed Actuary who will rely on the work, and with the Chief Investment Officer for the asset side.
Record the December 31 valuation date and the projection horizon (minimum through the end of the next contract year plus run-out).
checklist.done: a scope memo names every entity, segment, method and horizon, agreed by the Appointed Actuary and the CIO.

checklist.step: Assign and extract the supporting asset portfolio
actions: Extract the December 31 holdings by legal entity: book value, market value, coupon, maturity, call features, NAIC designation and asset class.
Assign assets to liability segments so that no asset supports two segments, and record the assignment rule used.
Confirm the assigned book value equals the segment's liability plus the allocated surplus and reconcile the total to the statement Schedule D and the general ledger.
Hand the assignment schedule and cash-flow file to the ALM actuary with a signed data reliance letter.
checklist.done: assets are uniquely assigned by segment, reconcile to Schedule D and the ledger, and come with a signed reliance letter.

checklist.step: Build the liability cash flows from the Part C reserve model
actions: Import the approved December 31 reserve exhibit and convert each segment's liability into a monthly payment pattern using the completion-factor lag profile.
Project the next contract year's claim outgo from the filed bid's projected allowed cost, member months and benefit design.
Layer in provider capitation payments on their contractual payment dates and quality-withhold releases on their settlement dates.
Reconcile the opening liability in the projection to the booked reserve to the dollar before running any scenario.
checklist.done: the liability cash-flow projection opens at exactly the booked reserve and carries a dated monthly payment pattern per segment.

checklist.step: Model the CMS revenue and settlement cash-flow timing
actions: Project the monthly CMS capitation receipt on its normal payment date, built from the county benchmark, the bid, the risk score and the rebate.
Add the risk-adjustment reconciliation cash flows on the mid-year and final sweep payment dates rather than spreading them evenly.
Add the Part C MLR remittance outflow on its CMS remittance date and any expected civil money penalty or recoupment.
Add the quality-bonus payment only for contracts eligible for it, and exclude it entirely for contracts carrying the low-performing icon.
checklist.done: CMS receipts and settlements are modelled on their actual payment dates, with quality bonus excluded for low-performing contracts.

checklist.step: Set the economic and interest-rate scenario set
actions: Run the prescribed deterministic interest-rate scenarios plus a stochastic set sized to the materiality of the interest-sensitive segments.
Add a liquidity scenario in which a CMS payment is suspended for one month under an enforcement action.
Add a credit scenario applying default and downgrade assumptions to the assigned portfolio by NAIC designation.
Record every scenario definition, its parameters and its rationale in the scenario register.
checklist.done: the scenario register defines each prescribed, liquidity and credit scenario with parameters and rationale.

checklist.step: Build the network-adequacy stress scenario from the CMS criteria
actions: Get from Network Management the latest CMS network adequacy submission: the Health Service Delivery tables and the automated criteria check results by county and provider or facility specialty type under 42 CFR 422.116.
List every county and specialty type failing the minimum-number or maximum time-and-distance standard, or covered only by an approved exception request.
Cost the failure: members in that county routed out of network, paid at the applicable Medicare rate plus any non-contracted differential, plus the appeal and grievance handling cost.
Model the resulting claim outgo increase as its own stress scenario and document the member counts and rates used.
checklist.done: a network-adequacy stress scenario exists, built from the actual failing counties and specialty types in the CMS criteria results.

checklist.step: Run the scenarios and capture the results
actions: Run every scenario in the register on the approved production model version and record the run identifier for each.
Capture for each scenario the ending surplus, the minimum interim cash position and the month it occurs.
Flag any scenario with a negative ending surplus or a negative interim cash position for the exception log immediately.
Store the run outputs against the run identifiers in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: every registered scenario has a stored run with ending surplus and minimum interim cash recorded, and failures are flagged.

checklist.step: Run the sensitivity set around the key assumptions
actions: Sensitise claim trend by plus 5% and plus 10% and record the effect on ending surplus.
Sensitise the risk score for a 3% reduction at the next CMS sweep and for a RADV extrapolated recovery.
Sensitise membership for a 10% attrition following a Star Ratings drop and the associated 42 CFR 422.2266(b) icon disclosure.
Tabulate each sensitivity against the base run so the reader sees which assumption the conclusion depends on.
checklist.done: a sensitivity table shows the effect of trend, risk score and membership shocks against the base run.

checklist.step: Document every assumption with its source
actions: Build an assumption register listing each assumption, its value, its source document, its owner and whether it changed from the prior year.
For each change, record the reason, the dollar effect on ending surplus and the approver.
Attach the source evidence — bid pricing exhibits, CMS rate announcement, investment yield curve, network criteria results — to the register rows.
Have the Chief Actuary approve the register before the memorandum is drafted.
checklist.done: every assumption has a value, a source, an owner and, where changed, a quantified effect and an approver.

checklist.step: Obtain independent peer review of the model and the results
actions: Confirm the model version used is the approved production version with no uncontrolled change since validation.
Re-run the base scenario and one failing scenario independently and compare ending surplus within a 1% tolerance.
Challenge in writing every assumption that changed from the prior year and every scenario whose result improved without an assumption reason.
Log the review and its conditions against the reporting year in the repository.
checklist.done: an independent reviewer has re-run base and failing scenarios within tolerance and challenged each assumption change in writing.

checklist.step: Reconcile the AAT starting position to the annual statement
actions: Tie the opening liability in the projection to Exhibit 6 and Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Part 2B in the draft blank.
Tie the assigned asset book value to Schedule D and to the assets page of the blank.
Explain and clear any difference with the Controller before the memorandum is finalised.
Attach the signed reconciliation to the AAT pack.
checklist.done: opening liabilities and assigned assets tie to the draft statement and the reconciliation is signed.

checklist.step: Draft the AAT memorandum
actions: Write the sections required by ASOP 22 and ASOP 7: purpose, scope and segmentation, asset assignment, liability cash flows, scenarios and their rationale, results, sensitivities, reliance and conclusion.
State the conclusion for each entity — assets make adequate provision, or they do not and an additional reserve of a stated amount is held.
Include the network-adequacy stress as a named scenario with the counties and specialty types that drove it.
File the memorandum with restricted access and link it to the opinion folder for the Appointed Actuary's reliance.
checklist.done: the memorandum carries every required section, a per-entity conclusion and the named network-adequacy scenario, and is linked to the opinion folder.

checklist.step: Take the conclusion and any additional reserve to governance
actions: Present the results table, failing scenarios and any proposed additional reserve to the Reserve Committee before the opinion is signed.
Where a scenario fails, present the options — hold additional reserve, reposition assets, or change the network or benefit design — with the owner of each.
Record the committee's decision and the approved additional reserve, if any, in the minutes.
Notify the Appointed Actuary of the approved position in writing so the opinion reflects it.
checklist.done: the committee has minuted a decision on every failing scenario and the Appointed Actuary holds it in writing before signature.

checklist.step: Trigger an interim refresh when the business changes materially
actions: Set the named triggers: a service area expansion or reduction, a network termination that fails a 42 CFR 422.116 county standard, a Star Ratings change that removes the quality bonus, and a CMS enforcement action suspending payment or enrollment.
Subscribe to the Network Management and Compliance distribution lists so the triggers reach the actuary without being asked for.
On a trigger, re-run the affected scenarios within 30 days and report the revised conclusion to the Chief Actuary.
Log each trigger, its date, the re-run and the outcome in the AAT pack.
checklist.done: every named trigger has a subscription, a 30-day re-run commitment and a logged outcome when it fires.

checklist.step: Archive the AAT pack under the 10-year retention label
actions: File the scope memo, asset assignment, cash-flow builds, scenario register, run outputs, sensitivity table, assumption register, peer review, reconciliation, memorandum and committee minutes under REG-051-C04 and the reporting year.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm the pack is searchable by legal entity, reporting year and scenario name.
checklist.done: the complete AAT pack is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by entity, year and scenario.

testing.step: Rebuild the AAT scope population and reconcile it
actions: List the legal entities and liability segments carrying reserves at December 31 from the approved reserve exhibit, independently of the AAT scope memo.
Compare to the segments actually tested and treat any reserved segment left untested as an exception.
Confirm the projection horizon covers at least the next contract year plus run-out for each segment.
Sign the scope population as complete in the workpaper.
testing.done: every reserved segment is either tested or logged as an out-of-scope exception, and the horizon is confirmed.

testing.step: Test the asset assignment and reconcile it to Schedule D
actions: Pull the December 31 holdings independently from the investment system by legal entity.
Confirm no asset is assigned to more than one liability segment and that the assignment rule was applied consistently.
Reconcile assigned book value to the statement Schedule D total and to the general ledger investment balance.
Confirm a signed data reliance letter exists from the investment data owner.
testing.done: assets reconcile to Schedule D and the ledger, are uniquely assigned, and are covered by a signed reliance letter.

testing.step: Re-tie the liability projection to the booked reserve
actions: Read the opening liability in each scenario run output and compare it to the approved December 31 reserve exhibit by segment.
Compare the monthly payment pattern to the completion-factor lag profile used in the reserve model.
Confirm the next-year claim outgo is built from the filed bid's projected allowed cost and member months, and trace two figures to the bid exhibits.
Any opening difference is an exception with the dollar amount recorded.
testing.done: each projection opens at the booked reserve, uses the reserve model's lag profile, and traces to the filed bid.

testing.step: Draw and document the scenario sample for re-performance
actions: Take 100% of failing scenarios, 100% of the network-adequacy stress and the base scenario.
Draw four further scenarios at random from the register using a recorded seed.
Record the register size, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every scenario that failed in the prior year as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: the scenario sample is reproducible, covers all failures and the network stress, and carries prior-year failures forward.

testing.step: Re-run the sampled scenarios independently
actions: Re-run each sampled scenario from the assumption register on the approved production model version without opening the original output.
Compare ending surplus and minimum interim cash to the recorded result within a 1% tolerance.
Confirm the run identifier stored in the repository matches the output relied on in the memorandum.
A conclusion that flips on re-run is escalated to the Chief Actuary the same day.
testing.done: each sampled scenario re-runs within tolerance against the stored run identifier, or the difference is escalated.

testing.step: Recompute the network-adequacy stress from the CMS criteria results
actions: Obtain the CMS network adequacy criteria results and Health Service Delivery tables directly from Network Management for the same submission date.
Independently list the counties and specialty types failing the minimum-number or time-and-distance standards under 42 CFR 422.116, including those covered only by an exception request.
Compare the list to the counties and specialty types used in the stress scenario and quantify anything omitted.
Recompute the out-of-network cost for two failing counties using the members enrolled and the applicable Medicare rate.
testing.done: the failing county and specialty list independently matches the stress inputs, and the recomputed cost for two counties agrees within tolerance.

testing.step: Test the assumption register and change control
actions: Confirm every assumption used in the sampled runs appears in the register with a source document attached.
For each assumption changed from the prior year, confirm the reason, the quantified effect and the approver are recorded.
Confirm the model version used was the approved production version and no change was made outside change control between the runs and the opinion signature.
An assumption with no source, or a change with no approver, is a fail.
testing.done: every sampled assumption is sourced and every change is quantified and approved, on an unchanged production model version.

testing.step: Verify governance, reliance and timing against the opinion
actions: Confirm the AAT runs and peer review completed before the actuarial opinion signature date; work completed afterwards cannot support the opinion.
Confirm the Reserve Committee minutes record a decision on every failing scenario and the additional reserve, if any, that was booked.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary holds written notice of the approved position and that the memorandum is linked from the opinion folder.
Confirm interim-refresh triggers fired during the year were re-run within 30 days and logged.
testing.done: AAT completion pre-dates the opinion, failures are minuted with decisions, and every fired trigger has a logged 30-day re-run.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, segment or scenario, and the effect on the adequacy conclusion.
Assign a root cause (segment omitted from scope, asset double-assigned, stale bid inputs, network criteria not refreshed, run after opinion signature, assumption unapproved) and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next October 1 assumption-setting checkpoint.
Where the exception could change the adequacy conclusion, notify the Appointed Actuary and Regulatory Counsel the same day for an opinion supportability assessment.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date before the next cycle, with opinion supportability assessed where relevant.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against the requirement that every scenario ends with positive surplus or carries a booked additional reserve.
Have the independent reviewer, who built no liability projection and set no assumption under test, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any adequacy risk to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
File the workpaper under REG-051-C04 with the reporting year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
