Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi) (compliance program elements requiring effective monitoring and auditing of data used for payment), 42 CFR 422.137(d) and 42 CFR 422.101(b) read on eCFR; the reconciliation is the monitoring control that evidences complete and accurate membership and claims data behind the reserve

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly reconciliation of member months, enrollment status, risk scores, paid claims and capitation payments between the Policy Administration Platform, the Claims Platform, the CMS MARx Monthly Membership Report and Transaction Reply Report, and the actuarial reserve extract, for every H-contract and PBP

In-scope systems.value: Enrollment of record in the policy administration system, claims in the Claims Platform, CMS truth in the MARx MMR/TRR/MOR files, all landed in the warehouse and compared in the reconciliation job

Compliance procedure documented.value: Part C Reserve Data Reconciliation Procedure — source extraction and control totals, member-month comparison to MMR, TRR retroactivity handling, claims-to-GL tie, risk-score comparison to MOR, variance thresholds, break assignment and sign-off

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Data Officer and the Chief Actuary; re-approved annually and on any MARx file layout change announced by HPMS memo or any policy administration system release affecting enrollment records

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Reconciliation complete and signed by WD-4 of each quarterly valuation close (April, July, October, January); enrollment discrepancies raised to CMS through the MARx Retroactive Processing Contractor within 30 days of identification

Deadline reminders configured.value: Warehouse job scheduler alerts when the MMR/TRR files land each month, plus reconciliation calendar reminders at WD-6 (extract complete), WD-5 (breaks assigned) and WD-4 (sign-off due) each quarter

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Control totals, comparison output, break register with disposition, retroactivity submissions to CMS and the signed acceptance retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any contract-month member-month variance above 0.5%, any unexplained claims-to-GL difference, any risk score not traceable to a MOR sweep, and any break left unassigned at sign-off is logged with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CDO signs off systemic breaks that recur across two consecutive quarters and any remediation requiring a policy administration system change

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every contract-month in the experience period for every H-contract and PBP, across the four reconciliation dimensions: member months, enrollment status, paid claims and risk score

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Member months within 0.5% per contract-month, claims three-way tie to the dollar after named reconciling items, risk scores fully traceable to a named MOR sweep; any breach outside these, or any unassigned break at sign-off, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the test runs each quarter over the full contract-month population and adds a full-year look-back at Q4 covering retroactive enrollment activity

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not run the reconciliation job or own any of the source systems being compared

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly reserve data reconciliation test workpaper (control totals, independent re-extraction, break register review, retroactivity tracing) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C05 and the valuation date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed reconciliation with control totals, break register and CMS retroactivity submissions, producible for a CMS program audit data-integrity request or a state DOI examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Officer routes CMS program audit data requests; enrollment discrepancies go to CMS through the MARx Retroactive Processing Contractor, and the Chief Data Officer signs any statement about systemic data quality before it is sent

checklist.step: Extract enrollment of record from the policy administration system
actions: Run the quarterly enrollment extract for every H-contract and PBP: member identifier including MBI, effective and termination dates, plan benefit package, county of residence and dual/LIS status by month.
Record control totals — distinct members, member months, and count of records with a retroactive effective date — on the reconciliation control sheet.
Exclude nothing at extraction; suppression happens in the comparison layer where it is visible.
Land the extract in the warehouse with the run identifier and the extract timestamp.
checklist.done: the enrollment extract is landed with control totals recorded and the run identifier logged.

checklist.step: Load the CMS MARx membership and transaction files
actions: Download from MARx the Monthly Membership Report (MMR), the Monthly Membership Detail and the Transaction Reply Report (TRR) for every month in the experience period.
Load each file into the warehouse with the payment month, the contract and the file received date preserved.
Confirm every expected month is present — a missing MMR month silently understates member months — and alert Enrollment Operations on any gap.
Record the CMS control totals (member months, payment amount) per contract-month on the control sheet.
checklist.done: every expected MMR, membership detail and TRR month is loaded with CMS control totals recorded and gaps alerted.

checklist.step: Compare member months contract-month by contract-month
actions: Join the policy administration extract to the MMR on contract, PBP, payment month and member identifier.
Produce a variance table showing internal member months, CMS member months, absolute difference and percentage difference for each contract-month.
Flag every contract-month over the 0.5% threshold and every member present in one source but not the other.
Publish the variance table to the reconciliation dashboard for the Reserving Actuary before the model run.
checklist.done: a contract-month variance table exists with every breach over 0.5% and every one-sided member flagged.

checklist.step: Work the enrollment breaks by category
actions: Classify each one-sided member: CMS-only (plan missed an enrollment), internal-only (CMS rejected or never processed), retroactive addition, retroactive termination, or duplicate/overlapping coverage.
For internal-only members, find the rejecting TRR transaction reply code and correct the submission or the member record accordingly.
For CMS-only members, add or reinstate the record in the policy administration system so claims can adjudicate correctly.
Record the category, the member count and the action on the break register with an owner and a due date.
checklist.done: every one-sided member is categorised, has a named action with an owner and due date, and appears on the break register.

checklist.step: Submit unresolved enrollment discrepancies to CMS
actions: Where the plan's record is right and CMS's is not, prepare a retroactive enrollment change request to the CMS Retroactive Processing Contractor with the member, contract, period and supporting documentation.
Submit within 30 days of identifying the discrepancy and record the submission date and case reference on the break register.
Track each case to the CMS response and confirm the correction appears in a later MMR before closing it.
Escalate cases open beyond 90 days to the Compliance Officer with the enrollment and revenue effect quantified.
checklist.done: every discrepancy needing CMS action is submitted within 30 days with a case reference, tracked to a corrected MMR.

checklist.step: Tie paid claims across the claims system, the extract and the ledger
actions: Run the claims system paid control report for the cut date by incurred month and benefit category.
Compare to the actuarial extract totals and to the general ledger claims-paid account for the same period.

Itemise every reconciling item — voids and reissues, refunds and overpayment recoveries, capitation paid outside claims, Part D excluded, pharmacy carve-out, subrogation recoveries — with its dollar amount.
Sign the three-way tie and attach it to the reconciliation pack.
checklist.done: the three-way claims tie balances with every reconciling item named and quantified, and is signed.

checklist.step: Reconcile risk scores to the CMS Model Output Report
actions: Extract the risk scores used in the revenue and accrual calculations by member and payment year.
Compare them to the MOR risk scores for the same members and payment year, and to the risk score field on the MMR.
Explain any difference by sweep timing, and confirm the sweep date relied on is named in the reserve workpaper.
Flag any score that cannot be traced to a MOR line as an exception, since it cannot support a booked receivable.
checklist.done: every risk score used in the accrual traces to a named MOR sweep line, or is flagged as untraceable.

checklist.step: Reconcile CMS capitation receipts to the revenue ledger
actions: Total the MMR payment amounts by contract and payment month and compare to premium revenue recognised in the ledger.
Reconcile the difference through the MMR adjustment reason codes: retroactive adjustments, risk-score true-ups, Part D-related amounts and low-income subsidy items.
Confirm the cash received in the bank matches the MMR payment total for the month, and investigate any unapplied cash.
Attach the revenue reconciliation to the quarterly close binder.
checklist.done: CMS payments per the MMR reconcile to recognised revenue and to bank cash, with adjustment reason codes explaining the difference.

checklist.step: Test the retroactivity population separately
actions: Isolate all enrollment records with a retroactive effective or termination date processed in the quarter.
Quantify their effect on member months in each affected prior month and confirm the reserve model picked up the restated months.
Confirm claims already paid for retroactively terminated members are flagged for recovery with Claims Operations.
Report the retroactivity dollar effect to the Reserving Actuary so the roll-forward explains it rather than absorbing it.
checklist.done: the retroactivity population is quantified, reflected in restated member months, and reported to the Reserving Actuary.

checklist.step: Assess and clear the break register against thresholds
actions: Review every open break against the 0.5% member-month and dollar-tie thresholds and mark it cleared, accepted with rationale, or escalated.
Require a written rationale, not a tolerance reference alone, for anything accepted uncleared.
Escalate any break recurring for two consecutive quarters to the Chief Data Officer as systemic.
Confirm no break is left unassigned before sign-off.
checklist.done: every break is cleared, accepted with a written rationale, or escalated, and none is unassigned.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial acceptance of the reconciled data
actions: Read the variance table, the three-way claims tie, the risk-score trace and the open break register before the model run.
Decide whether the data is fit for valuation, and where a break is material, adjust the model input and document the adjustment rather than ignoring the break.
Sign the data acceptance on the reconciliation control sheet with the date and the run identifier of the extract accepted.
Refuse acceptance where an unassigned break remains, and hold the model run.
checklist.done: the Reserving Actuary has signed acceptance naming the accepted run identifier, with every material break either adjusted or explained.

checklist.step: Publish the reconciliation results to the stakeholders
actions: Publish the quarter's variance trend, break counts by category and open CMS retroactivity cases to the data quality dashboard.
Send the summary to the Chief Actuary, the Controller and Enrollment Operations within one business day of sign-off.
Highlight categories that grew quarter over quarter with the named owner for each.
Book the systemic items into the next quarter's remediation plan.
checklist.done: the dashboard is refreshed and the summary sent to actuarial, finance and enrollment owners within one business day of sign-off.

checklist.step: Fix the root cause in the source system
actions: For each systemic break, raise a change request against the responsible system with the break category, volume and financial effect.
Prioritise fixes that prevent recurrence — TRR reply-code auto-handling, retroactive date validation, duplicate coverage detection — over manual clean-up.
Agree the release date with the system owner and record it on the break register.
Confirm after release that the break category volume falls in the following quarter's reconciliation.
checklist.done: every systemic break has a raised change request, an agreed release date and a measured volume reduction after release.

checklist.step: Run the annual full-year look-back at Q4
actions: Re-reconcile all twelve months of the year at Q4 rather than only the quarter, so retroactive activity applied late is caught.
Compare the restated full-year member months to those used in the MLR calculation and the bid experience submission.
Report any restatement affecting a filed figure to the Appointed Actuary and Regulatory Reporting the same week.
File the look-back with the year-end valuation pack.
checklist.done: a full-year re-reconciliation is completed at Q4 and any restatement affecting a filed figure is reported the same week.

checklist.step: Archive the reconciliation pack under the 10-year retention label
actions: File the control sheets, variance tables, break register, CMS retroactivity submissions, three-way claims tie, risk-score trace and signed acceptance under REG-051-C05 and the valuation date.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm the pack is searchable by H-contract number, payment month and break category.
checklist.done: the reconciliation pack is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by contract, month and break category.

testing.step: Rebuild the contract-month population independently
actions: List every H-contract and PBP active in the experience period from the MARx contract roster rather than from the reconciliation output.
Build the expected contract-month grid and confirm the reconciliation covered every cell, including months with zero enrollment.
Confirm every expected MMR and TRR month is present in the warehouse with its file received date.
Sign the population as complete and record the cell count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the contract-month grid is complete against the MARx roster, every CMS file month is present, and the population is signed.

testing.step: Re-extract the sources independently and compare control totals
actions: Re-run the enrollment extract from the policy administration system for the same cut date without using the reconciliation job.
Re-total member months and distinct members and compare to the control sheet figures.
Re-total MMR member months from the raw CMS files and compare to the CMS control totals recorded.
Any difference in control totals means the reconciliation ran on a different population and is an exception.
testing.done: independently re-extracted control totals match the recorded control sheet on both the internal and CMS sides.

testing.step: Draw and document the break sample
actions: Take 100% of contract-months breaching the 0.5% threshold and 100% of breaks accepted uncleared.
Draw 25 individual member-level breaks at random across the categories using a recorded seed.
Record the register size, the seed and the selection date for reproducibility.
Add every break open from the prior quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all threshold breaches and accepted breaks, and retests prior-quarter items.

testing.step: Re-perform the member-month variance for the sampled contract-months
actions: Independently join the re-extracted enrollment to the raw MMR for the sampled contract-months and recompute the variance percentage.
Compare the recomputed variance to the published variance table and explain any difference in the join logic.
Confirm the members driving the variance are the same members identified on the break register.
A variance that only appears on independent recomputation indicates a join defect and is an exception.
testing.done: recomputed variances agree with the published table and the driving members match the break register.

testing.step: Trace sampled breaks to their disposition and CMS submission
actions: For each sampled break, read the category, owner, action and closure evidence on the register.
Where CMS action was needed, confirm a retroactive change request was submitted within 30 days of identification and a case reference recorded.
Confirm closure is evidenced by the correction appearing in a later MMR, not by an internal note alone.
A break closed without corroborating source evidence is a fail.
testing.done: every sampled break has an evidenced disposition, and CMS-facing breaks show a 30-day submission and a corrected MMR.

testing.step: Re-perform the three-way claims tie
actions: Pull the claims-paid ledger balance and the claims system paid total independently for the same cut date.
Recompute the tie and test each named reconciling item to supporting detail — void and reissue reports, recovery postings, capitation payment runs.
Confirm Part D and pharmacy carve-out exclusions are applied consistently and are not being used to absorb unexplained differences.
Any reconciling item without supporting detail is an exception at its full dollar value.
testing.done: the three-way tie re-performs and every reconciling item is supported by named detail.

testing.step: Test risk-score traceability and the retroactivity population
actions: Select 20 members and trace each risk score used in the accrual to a specific MOR line for the correct payment year and sweep.
Re-isolate the retroactive enrollment population for the quarter from the raw source and compare its member-month effect to the figure reported to the Reserving Actuary.
Confirm claims paid for retroactively terminated members were flagged for recovery with Claims Operations.
Log any untraceable score or unreported retroactivity effect as an exception.
testing.done: sampled risk scores trace to named MOR lines and the retroactivity effect independently matches what was reported to actuarial.

testing.step: Verify the acceptance, thresholds and timing controls
actions: Confirm the Reserving Actuary's signed acceptance names the run identifier actually used in the valuation model.
Confirm the acceptance date is before the model run and by WD-4 of the close.
Confirm no break was unassigned at acceptance and that every accepted-uncleared break carries a written rationale rather than a tolerance reference.
Confirm breaks recurring across two quarters were escalated to the Chief Data Officer.
testing.done: the acceptance names the used run identifier, pre-dates the model run, and no break was unassigned or accepted without a written rationale.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the contract, month, dimension and the reserve or revenue effect.
Assign a root cause (extract scope, join defect, missing CMS file month, TRR reply code unhandled, retroactivity not restated, unsupported reconciling item) and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarterly cycle and require a change request where the fix is systemic.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, a remediation date inside the next cycle and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the 0.5% member-month threshold and the dollar-tie requirement.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither ran the reconciliation nor owns a compared source system, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Data Governance Council and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper under REG-051-C05 with the valuation date.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
