Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi) (compliance program duty to respond promptly to detected offenses and to cooperate with CMS monitoring), 42 CFR 422.137(d) and 42 CFR 422.101(b) read on eCFR at intake of each inquiry, together with the CMS Program Audit Protocols and the domiciliary state's examination statute

In-scope processes.value: Intake, routing, drafting, clearance, transmission and closure of every regulator inquiry touching valuation: CMS bid desk-review questions in HPMS, CMS program audit universe and reserve requests, RADV audit correspondence, state DOI financial examination interrogatories and analyst questions on the filed opinion

In-scope systems.value: Every inquiry logged in the tracker with source, receipt date and due date; supporting extracts produced from the reserving platform and the warehouse; responses transmitted through HPMS, the state's secure portal or the examiner's request system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulator Valuation Inquiry Response Procedure — same-day logging, clock calculation, owner routing, evidence assembly, actuarial drafting, counsel clearance, transmission, acknowledgement capture and post-response lessons

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Actuary; refreshed on each new CMS Program Audit Protocol release and after every completed examination

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Default response within 30 days of receipt unless the regulator states otherwise; CMS bid desk-review questions answered by the date in the HPMS desk-review message, often 3 to 5 business days during the June to August bid review; program audit universes submitted within the days stated in the engagement letter; examination interrogatories per the examiner's schedule

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tracker alerts at day 1 (owner assigned), day 10 (draft due), day 20 (counsel clearance due) and day 25 (transmission due) against a 30-day clock, with an accelerated schedule auto-applied when the stated deadline is under 10 days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Inbound request, evidence pack produced, drafts, counsel clearance, transmitted response and regulator acknowledgement retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d) and for the duration of any open examination

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any inquiry logged late, any response sent after its deadline, any response sent without counsel clearance where required, and any inconsistency between a response and a previously filed figure is logged with disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every late response, every correction to a previously sent answer and every self-disclosure arising from an inquiry

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every valuation-related regulator inquiry received in the period from CMS (HPMS desk review, program audit, RADV) and from state insurance departments (examination interrogatories, analyst questions on the opinion), whether closed or open

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of inquiries logged the day received and answered on or before the stated deadline; any missed deadline, any unlogged inquiry found in a mailbox, and any answer contradicting a filed figure without a correction is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs quarterly over all inquiries received in the quarter, with 100% coverage rather than sampling given the volume

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, cleared or transmitted any inquiry response in the period under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly regulator inquiry test workpaper (inquiry population from tracker and mailbox sweep, clock recomputation, clearance checks, consistency tracing) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C06

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Full inquiry file per request — inbound message, evidence pack, final response, transmission receipt and acknowledgement — producible on demand during an examination or program audit within 2 business days

Regulator response path.value: All CMS valuation correspondence goes through the HPMS contact of record with the Compliance Officer copied; state inquiries go through the Regulatory Reporting Manager; Regulatory Counsel clears anything conceding an error, a late filing or a reserve inadequacy before it leaves

checklist.step: Log every inbound valuation inquiry the day it arrives
actions: Monitor the monitored regulatory mailbox, the HPMS message inbox and the examiner's request portal each business morning.

Create a tracker item the same day with: source (CMS HPMS desk review, CMS program audit, RADV, state examination, state analyst), regulator name, contract or entity, date received and the deadline the regulator stated.
Attach the inbound message and every attachment exactly as received, with no reformatting.
Notify the Appointed Actuary and the Compliance Officer within 4 hours of logging.
checklist.done: every inquiry has a same-day tracker item with source, stated deadline, attachments and a notification to the actuary and compliance.

checklist.step: Compute the response clock and set the internal milestones
actions: Read the regulator's stated deadline; where none is stated, apply the 30-day default from receipt and record that basis on the item.
Count calendar or business days exactly as the regulator expressed them and write the computed due date on the tracker item.
Set internal milestones at day 10 (draft), day 20 (clearance) and day 25 (transmission); where the stated deadline is under 10 days, apply the accelerated schedule immediately.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance the same day if the stated deadline is not achievable with the evidence required.
checklist.done: each item carries a computed due date, a stated basis, internal milestones and an escalation where the deadline is unachievable.

checklist.step: Route the inquiry to the accountable owner
actions: Assign reserve, completion factor, margin and adequacy questions to the Appointed Actuary; bid pricing questions to the Pricing Actuary; data and membership questions to the Data Quality Manager; statement presentation questions to the Controller.
Name a single accountable owner per item — never a team — and a named backup for absence.
Record on the item which other functions must contribute and by when.
Confirm the owner has accepted the item in the tracker within one business day.
checklist.done: each inquiry has one named accountable owner who has accepted it, plus a backup and a contributor list.

checklist.step: Read the question precisely and scope the answer
actions: Break the request into numbered sub-questions and restate each in the response outline so nothing is answered by implication.
Identify the exact period, entity, contract and statement line each sub-question covers.
Where the question is ambiguous, submit a written clarification request through the same channel and log the date asked and answered — do not guess at scope.
Agree the outline with the Compliance Officer before the evidence pack is assembled.
checklist.done: a numbered response outline exists covering every sub-question with its period, entity and statement line, agreed with compliance.

checklist.step: Assemble the evidence pack from the source systems
actions: Pull the exhibits the question needs: triangles, completion factors, roll-forward, PDR test, assumption memo, reconciliation and the filed statement page.
Regenerate the figures from the archived valuation pack for the period in question rather than from the current quarter's run.
Label every exhibit with the entity, period, run identifier and the date produced so the regulator can pin it to a filing.
List the exhibits in an index that maps each one to the numbered sub-question it answers.
checklist.done: an indexed evidence pack maps labelled exhibits, regenerated from the archived valuation, to each numbered sub-question.

checklist.step: Check the draft answer against everything previously filed
actions: Compare each figure in the draft to the filed annual and quarterly statements, the signed opinion and the bid submitted for the same period.
Where a figure differs because of a later restatement, say so explicitly with the restatement date and cause rather than presenting the newer number silently.
Check the answer does not contradict a previous response to the same regulator on the same subject; pull the prior inquiry files to confirm.
Record the consistency check on the tracker item with the documents compared.
checklist.done: every figure in the draft is reconciled to what was filed, with restatements disclosed and prior responses checked for contradiction.

checklist.step: Answer CMS bid desk-review questions inside the HPMS window
actions: Open the desk-review message in the HPMS bid module and read the CMS actuary's question and the stated response date, often 3 to 5 business days in the June to August review.
Prepare the answer against the submitted Bid Pricing Tool worksheet and cell the question references, and quantify any resubmission effect on the bid.
Have the Chief Actuary review before submission, since a bid resubmission changes the benefit package filed for the contract year.
Submit through HPMS, save the submission confirmation and record the CMS actuary's follow-up or acceptance on the tracker item.
checklist.done: each desk-review question is answered in HPMS within the stated window with a saved confirmation and a recorded CMS acceptance.

checklist.step: Produce program audit universes and reserve records on the audit clock
actions: On receipt of a CMS program audit engagement letter, read the universe list and the submission days stated in it and diarise each.
Assign each universe to its data owner with the record layout from the current CMS Program Audit Protocols and a validation step before submission.
Run the universe integrity checks CMS applies — record counts, date ranges, mandatory fields, valid code values — and fix defects before uploading rather than after rejection.
Upload through the audit portal, save the confirmation and log any CMS request for a corrected universe with its own clock.
checklist.done: every requested universe is validated against the CMS layout and uploaded within the engagement letter's stated days, with confirmations saved.

checklist.step: Handle RADV and payment-integrity requests
actions: Log the RADV sample list with the member identifiers, the payment year and the medical record submission deadline stated by CMS.
Coordinate with Medical Records and the provider network to retrieve the supporting records for each sampled HCC and track retrieval to the deadline.
Have the Appointed Actuary quantify the potential extrapolated recovery and confirm it against the audit-recoupment haircut already booked in the reserve.
Submit through the CMS-designated portal and log the confirmation and any CMS finding letter.
checklist.done: the RADV sample is retrieved and submitted by the CMS deadline, with the potential recovery quantified against the booked haircut.

checklist.step: Answer state examination interrogatories on the filed opinion
actions: Read the examiner's interrogatory and identify which opinion paragraph, exhibit or memorandum section it targets.
Answer with reference to the filed memorandum sections rather than writing new analysis, and provide the memorandum where the examiner has not been given it.
Where the examiner challenges an assumption, provide the assumption register row, the source evidence and the peer review comment on it.
Offer a call with the examining actuary where the answer is complex, and minute the call on the tracker item.
checklist.done: each interrogatory is answered against the filed memorandum with assumption sources and peer review evidence attached.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel clearance before transmission
actions: Read every response that concedes an error, a late filing, a reserve inadequacy or a data defect, and every response to a program audit finding.
Assess privilege, self-disclosure exposure and consistency with prior statements to the same regulator.
Record clearance, or required edits, in writing on the tracker item before day 20 of the clock.
Escalate to the General Counsel anything that could support an enforcement action or a civil money penalty.
checklist.done: every response requiring clearance carries written counsel clearance on the tracker item before transmission.

checklist.step: Transmit the response through the regulator's own channel
actions: Send through the channel the regulator specified — HPMS message, the examiner's secure portal, or the state's filing system — never by ordinary email if a channel was named.
Include the numbered response, the indexed evidence pack and a cover note listing what is attached.
Capture the transmission receipt with its timestamp and attach it to the tracker item.
Confirm receipt with the regulator's contact where the channel gives no automatic acknowledgement.
checklist.done: the response is sent through the named channel with an indexed pack and a captured, timestamped transmission receipt.

checklist.step: Track the inquiry to acknowledgement and closure
actions: Record the regulator's acknowledgement, follow-up question or finding on the item and open a new clocked item for each follow-up.
Close the item only on an acknowledgement or a stated closure by the regulator, never on the fact of sending.
Where a finding results, link the item to the corrective action plan and its owner.
Report open items over 20 days old to the Head of Compliance weekly.
checklist.done: no item is closed without regulator acknowledgement, every follow-up has its own clock, and ageing items are reported weekly.

checklist.step: Feed findings back into the valuation process
actions: Review every inquiry closed in the quarter for the underlying cause: an unclear disclosure, an assumption the regulator does not accept, or a data defect.
Where a regulator has challenged an assumption, table it at the Reserve Committee for reconsideration with the challenge on the record.
Update the memorandum template or the disclosure wording where the same question keeps being asked.
Record the process change and its owner on the closed item.
checklist.done: every closed inquiry has a recorded cause and, where the regulator challenged an assumption or disclosure, a tabled process change.

checklist.step: Archive the inquiry file under the 10-year retention label
actions: File the inbound request, outline, evidence pack, drafts, counsel clearance, transmitted response, receipt and acknowledgement under REG-051-C06 and the inquiry reference.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d) and a legal hold while any examination or audit remains open.
Confirm the file is searchable by regulator, contract, entity and inquiry date.
checklist.done: the complete inquiry file is archived under a 10-year label with a hold where an examination is open, retrievable by regulator and date.

testing.step: Build the inquiry population and sweep for unlogged items
actions: Export every valuation-related inquiry item logged in the quarter with source, receipt date, due date, owner and status.
Sweep the monitored regulatory mailbox, the HPMS message history and the examiner portal for the same period and identify anything not in the tracker.
Every unlogged inquiry found in the sweep is an automatic exception, regardless of whether it was answered.
Sign the population as complete and record both counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: the tracker population is reconciled to an independent mailbox, HPMS and portal sweep, with every unlogged item raised.

testing.step: Recompute the response clock for every inquiry
actions: Read the deadline the regulator stated in the inbound message and compare it to the due date recorded on the item.
Where no deadline was stated, confirm the 30-day default from receipt was applied and the basis recorded.
Recompute elapsed days from receipt to transmission using the regulator's own calendar or business-day convention.
Any response transmitted after its recomputed due date is a fail, whether or not the regulator objected.
testing.done: every inquiry has a recomputed due date and elapsed-day result, and every late transmission is recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Verify same-day logging against the inbound timestamps
actions: Compare the inbound message timestamp on each attachment to the tracker item creation timestamp.
Confirm the actuary and compliance notification went out within 4 hours of logging.
Log any item created more than one business day after receipt as an exception, since the clock started before the item existed.
Record the distribution of logging lags in the workpaper as a trend measure.
testing.done: logging lag is measured against inbound timestamps for every item and items logged late are raised.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample for substantive re-performance
actions: Take 100% of CMS program audit, RADV and bid desk-review items and 100% of items answered after their due date.
Draw 10 further items at random across state analyst and examination questions using a recorded seed.
Record the population size, the seed and the selection date for reproducibility.
Add every prior-quarter exception item as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all CMS and late items, and retests prior-quarter exceptions.

testing.step: Re-read each sampled response against the question asked
actions: Break the inbound request into sub-questions independently and check each is answered explicitly in the response.
Identify sub-questions answered by implication, deferred, or silently dropped and record them as incomplete responses.
Confirm the evidence index maps an exhibit to every sub-question that required one.
Confirm any clarification request to the regulator is logged with the date asked and answered.
testing.done: every sampled sub-question is explicitly answered and evidenced, or the gap is recorded as an incomplete response.

testing.step: Trace sampled figures back to the filed record
actions: Take three figures from each sampled response and trace them to the filed statement page, the signed opinion or the submitted Bid Pricing Tool for the same period.
Where the response figure differs, confirm a restatement was disclosed with its date and cause rather than substituted silently.
Compare the response to any earlier response to the same regulator on the same subject and look for contradiction.
An undisclosed difference from a filed figure is a reportable failure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: sampled figures trace to filed records with every difference disclosed, and no contradiction with earlier responses is found.

testing.step: Test clearance, channel and receipt evidence
actions: For each sampled response conceding an error, a late filing or a reserve inadequacy, confirm written Regulatory Counsel clearance pre-dates transmission.
Confirm the response went through the channel the regulator named and that a timestamped transmission receipt is attached.
Confirm the item was closed on a regulator acknowledgement, not on the fact of sending.
A response transmitted outside the named channel or without a receipt is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled response evidences pre-transmission clearance where required, the named channel, a receipt and an acknowledgement-based closure.

testing.step: Test CMS universe validation and RADV timeliness
actions: For each program audit universe submitted, re-run the CMS integrity checks — record counts, date range, mandatory fields, valid code values — against the file as submitted.
Compare the submission date to the days stated in the engagement letter and record any CMS request for a corrected universe as a quality exception.
For RADV, confirm every sampled medical record was submitted by the CMS deadline and that unretrieved records were escalated.
Compare the quantified potential extrapolated recovery to the audit-recoupment haircut booked in the reserve.
testing.done: universes re-validate against the CMS layout and were timely, RADV records met the deadline, and the recovery estimate ties to the booked haircut.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the regulator, inquiry reference, what failed and the enforcement exposure.
Assign a root cause (mailbox not swept, clock miscounted, owner not accepted, evidence regenerated from the wrong period, clearance skipped, wrong channel) and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarter and require a procedure change where the same cause recurs.
Where a response contradicted a filed figure, open a correction and self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel the same day.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with a correction assessment opened where a filed figure was contradicted.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time response rate and the logging-lag distribution against the 100% same-day logging and on-time response thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, cleared or transmitted no response in the period, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-051-C06.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Marketing Compliance Analyst owns the required-disclosure content in every MA member material and marketing piece; the Insurance Product Manager owns the benefit content those disclosures describe

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.101(a),(b) (the plan must cover all Part A and Part B basic benefits other than hospice, consistent with national and local coverage determinations, which is what the Evidence of Coverage and Summary of Benefits must state) and 42 CFR 422.254(a) (bid-based benefit package) read on eCFR, plus the current CMS Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines chapter and the model documents released for the contract year

In-scope processes.value: Building the CMS-required disclosures into every MA member and prospect material for each contract year: Annual Notice of Change, Evidence of Coverage, Summary of Benefits, provider and pharmacy directories, enrollment forms, denial and appeal notices, and every marketing and communication piece submitted through the HPMS Marketing Module

In-scope systems.value: Material masters and approved templates held in the document repository with material IDs; benefit content sourced from the bid and the Policy Administration Platform; submissions and approvals recorded against the CMS HPMS Marketing Module material ID

Compliance procedure documented.value: MA Material Disclosure Build Procedure — model document intake, benefit content sourcing from the accepted bid, required-element checklist per material type, material ID assignment, HPMS submission and review-period observance, distribution release and withdrawal on CMS disapproval

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and the Chief Product Officer; re-approved each year on release of the contract-year Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines and model documents, and on any HPMS memo changing the required disclaimers

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: ANOC and EOC delivered to enrollees by September 30 for the following contract year; materials requiring prior approval submitted to HPMS with the 45-day review period before intended use; File-and-Use eligible materials submitted with the 5-day period observed; provider directory updates within 30 days of a network change

Deadline reminders configured.value: Material calendar reminders at June 1 (model documents ingested), July 15 (drafts complete), August 1 (HPMS submission for prior-approval materials), September 1 (print release) and September 20 (mail drop confirmed) against the September 30 ANOC/EOC deadline

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Approved material master with material ID, the required-element checklist, the HPMS submission and disposition record, the print proof and the distribution file retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any material distributed before its review period ended, any material missing a required disclosure, any CMS disapproval and its withdrawal action, and any benefit statement inconsistent with the accepted bid is logged with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Market Conduct Compliance Manager signs off every withdrawal, correction and re-issue of a distributed material and any member-facing correction notice

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every material with a material ID used in the contract year — ANOC, EOC, Summary of Benefits, directories, enrollment kits, denial and appeal notices, advertising and sales presentations — by contract and plan benefit package

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a material distributed before its review period ended, a missing required disclosure or disclaimer, a benefit statement that does not match the accepted bid, or a disapproved material still in circulation is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per material change; the test runs quarterly on materials released in the quarter and adds a full pre-Annual-Enrollment sweep in September covering 100% of ANOC, EOC and Summary of Benefits versions

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, checked or submitted any sampled material

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly material disclosure test workpaper (material population from HPMS and the repository, element checklist re-performance, bid consistency tracing, distribution date checks) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C07

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Material ID inventory with HPMS dispositions, the as-distributed PDF of each material, the required-element checklist and the distribution date file, producible for a CMS program audit or a state market conduct examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance owns CMS marketing review and program audit responses through HPMS; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission that a material was distributed early or without a required disclosure before it is sent

checklist.step: Ingest the contract-year CMS model documents and marketing guidance
actions: Download from HPMS and the CMS website the contract-year model ANOC, model EOC, Summary of Benefits template, the standardised provider directory template and the current Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines.
Redline the new models against last year's to list every changed required sentence, disclaimer and formatting instruction.
Circulate the redline to Product, Member Communications and Legal with the sections each must action and a response date.
File the models in the repository as the only permitted starting point for this year's materials.
checklist.done: the contract-year models are filed as the controlled source and a redline of every changed required element has been circulated with owners.

checklist.step: Source the benefit content from the accepted bid
actions: Take the CMS-accepted Bid Pricing Tool and Plan Benefit Package for each contract and PBP as the single source of benefit truth.
Extract cost sharing, deductibles, maximum out-of-pocket, supplemental benefits and network tier structure into the benefit content sheet keyed by PBP.

Confirm every Part A and Part B basic benefit required by 42 CFR 422.101(a),(b) other than hospice is represented in the benefit content, and that no coverage is stated more narrowly than the applicable national or local coverage determination.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary sign the benefit content sheet as agreeing to the accepted bid.
checklist.done: a signed benefit content sheet per PBP matches the accepted bid and covers every required basic benefit.

checklist.step: Build the required-element checklist for each material type
actions: Build a checklist per material type listing every element CMS requires: the plan name and contract/PBP number, the material ID, the CMS-required disclaimers, the TTY number, the non-discrimination notice and multi-language interpreter availability, the network and formulary change language, and the appeal rights language.

Add the Star Ratings elements: the Star Ratings disclosure and, where the contract has scored 2.5 stars or below for Part C or Part D for the last three years, the CMS low-performing icon and the prescribed low-performing statement on every material referencing Star Ratings.
Cite the guideline section or CFR paragraph next to each element so a reviewer can verify it, not just tick it.
Have Legal and Market Conduct Compliance approve the checklist before drafting starts.
checklist.done: an approved, citation-referenced required-element checklist exists per material type, including the low-performing icon rule.

checklist.step: Confirm each contract's Star Ratings status and icon obligation
actions: Pull the contract's Part C and Part D summary ratings for the last three rating years from the HPMS Star Ratings module.
Determine for each contract whether it has scored 2.5 or below for Part C or Part D in each of the last three years and therefore carries the low-performing icon obligation.
Publish a contract-level flag list to Product, Marketing and Member Communications and lock it so no material is built against a stale rating.
Where a contract is newly flagged, notify the Chief Product Officer and Actuarial the same day, since the quality bonus revenue assumption also changes.
checklist.done: a locked contract-level low-performing flag list, derived from three years of HPMS summary ratings, is published to every material owner.

checklist.step: Draft each material from the model and the benefit content
actions: Build each material from the CMS model file, keeping every standardised sentence verbatim and filling only the variable fields.
Populate benefit values from the signed benefit content sheet, never from last year's document or from a marketing brief.
Insert the low-performing icon and the prescribed statement on every material that references the contract's Star Ratings where the flag list says so.
Version the draft in the repository with the contract, PBP, material type and contract year in the file name.
checklist.done: each draft is built from the CMS model with verbatim standardised text, bid-sourced benefit values and the icon where required.

checklist.step: Run the required-element review against the checklist
actions: Review each draft line by line against the approved checklist and mark each element present, absent or non-conforming with the page reference.
Check the reading level, font size and formatting instructions the guidelines impose, including the minimum font size for member materials.
Return any draft with an absent or altered required sentence to the author rather than editing it silently, so the defect is recorded.
Sign the completed checklist and attach it to the material record.
checklist.done: each material has a signed element checklist with a page reference for every required element and no absent or altered required sentence.

checklist.step: Assign the material ID under the CMS naming convention
actions: Assign the material ID following the CMS convention of contract number, the plan's internal identifier and the year, with the suffix that indicates accepted or File-and-Use status.
Place the material ID where the guidelines require it on the piece, and record it on the material record and in the inventory.
Confirm no material ID is reused across contract years or across materially different versions.
Reconcile the inventory of assigned IDs to the materials actually built each week during the build season.
checklist.done: every material carries a unique, correctly formed material ID placed as required and recorded in the reconciled inventory.

checklist.step: Determine the CMS review route for each material
actions: Classify each material as requiring prior approval, as File-and-Use eligible, or as not requiring submission, citing the guideline section for the call.
Confirm File-and-Use eligibility depends on the organization's current eligibility status and that the status has not been withdrawn by CMS.
Record the applicable review period on the material record — the 45-day prior-approval period or the 5-day File-and-Use period — and compute the earliest permitted distribution date.
Escalate any material whose earliest permitted date falls after its business need date, so the schedule moves rather than the rule.
checklist.done: each material has a cited review route, a recorded review period and a computed earliest permitted distribution date.

checklist.step: Submit the materials through the HPMS Marketing Module
actions: Log in to HPMS and open the Marketing Module material submission screen for the contract year.
Upload each material with its material ID, material type, language, contract and PBP association and the submission category (prior approval or File-and-Use).
Capture the HPMS submission confirmation and the submission date on the material record, since the review clock runs from it.
Monitor the module daily for CMS status changes, comments and disapprovals through the review period.
checklist.done: every submitted material shows an HPMS confirmation and a recorded submission date, with the module monitored daily.

checklist.step: Hold distribution until the review period has run
actions: Configure every campaign, mail drop and web publication to be gated on the material record's earliest permitted distribution date.
Refuse any request to release early, including for sales events, and record the request and the refusal on the material record.
Confirm the print vendor and the fulfilment vendor also hold to the gated date, in writing, before the print run is released.
Release only after Market Conduct Compliance marks the material clear for distribution.
checklist.done: no channel can release a material before its earliest permitted date and every early-release request is recorded and refused.

checklist.step: Withdraw or correct anything CMS disapproves
actions: On a CMS disapproval or comment in HPMS, stop distribution across every channel the same day and record the stop time.
Recall printed stock from field agents, brokers and fulfilment, and remove the piece from the website, the member portal and every campaign.
Correct the material against the CMS comment, resubmit with a new material ID version and observe the review period again from the resubmission.
Where members already received the disapproved version, assess and, where required, issue a correction notice, and log the whole event with the number of members affected.
checklist.done: disapproved material is stopped and recalled the same day, corrected and resubmitted, with member impact quantified and a correction notice assessed.

checklist.step: Deliver the ANOC and EOC by the September 30 deadline
actions: Build the mailing population from the policy administration system: every enrollee active for the following contract year, with the correct PBP, language preference and alternate-format flag.
Reconcile the population to the MARx membership file before the mail file goes to the vendor.
Confirm the vendor's mail drop and electronic delivery dates land on or before September 30 and obtain the postal and delivery confirmation files.
Reconcile delivered counts to the mailing population and chase every undeliverable and every alternate-format request individually.
checklist.done: ANOC and EOC delivery is evidenced on or before September 30 for a population reconciled to MARx, with undeliverables individually chased.

checklist.step: Keep the provider and pharmacy directories current
actions: Take the weekly network change file from Network Management: additions, terminations, panel-status and address changes by county and specialty.
Update the online directory within the CMS-required timeframe of the change becoming known and refresh the printed directory at its next scheduled version.
Confirm the directory reflects the network that supports the 42 CFR 422.116 adequacy standards for the counties served, and flag any county whose directory now shows a gap.
Log each update batch with its date so the currency of the directory is provable at audit.
checklist.done: network changes reach the online directory within the required timeframe and every update batch is dated and logged.

checklist.step: Maintain the material inventory and its dispositions
actions: Maintain a single inventory of every material ID with contract, PBP, type, language, review route, submission date, disposition, earliest permitted date, actual first-use date and retirement date.
Reconcile the inventory to the HPMS material list monthly and resolve any material present in one and not the other.
Retire superseded versions so no obsolete piece stays available to agents or on the site.
Publish the inventory to Sales, Member Communications and Compliance each month.
checklist.done: the inventory reconciles monthly to HPMS, records first-use and retirement dates, and is published to the using teams.

checklist.step: Archive the material record under the 10-year retention label
actions: File the as-distributed PDF, the element checklist, the benefit content sheet, the HPMS submission and disposition record, the print proof and the distribution file under REG-051-C07, the contract and the contract year.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm the record is searchable by material ID, contract number, PBP and contract year.
checklist.done: each material record is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by material ID, contract and year.

testing.step: Build the material population from HPMS and the repository
actions: Export the HPMS Marketing Module material list for the contract year with material ID, type, submission date and disposition.
Export the repository inventory for the same period and compare the two lists in both directions.
Sweep the member portal, the public website and the agent portal for any piece in circulation whose material ID appears on neither list.
Sign the population as complete and record every one-sided item as an exception.
testing.done: the population reconciles HPMS, the repository and what is actually in circulation, with every one-sided item raised.

testing.step: Draw and document the material sample
actions: Take 100% of ANOC, EOC and Summary of Benefits versions, 100% of materials from contracts on the low-performing flag list, and 100% of CMS-disapproved materials.
Draw 20 further materials at random across advertising, sales presentations, directories and member letters using a recorded seed.
Record the population size, the seed and the selection date for reproducibility.
Add every material that failed in the prior quarter as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all core member documents, low-performing contracts and disapprovals, and retests prior failures.

testing.step: Re-perform the required-element review on the as-distributed piece
actions: Work from the as-distributed PDF, not the approved draft, so any late edit is caught.

Check each element on the approved checklist independently — plan name and contract/PBP number, material ID, CMS disclaimers, TTY number, non-discrimination and multi-language notice, appeal rights, font size — and record the page reference.
Confirm every standardised CMS model sentence appears verbatim by comparing against the model file rather than by reading for sense.
Any absent, altered or reworded required sentence is a fail.
testing.done: each sampled as-distributed piece has an independent element result with page references and a verbatim comparison to the model.

testing.step: Re-derive the low-performing icon obligation and check its application
actions: Pull the Part C and Part D summary ratings for the last three rating years for every contract directly from the HPMS Star Ratings module.
Independently determine which contracts have scored 2.5 or below for three consecutive years and compare to the published flag list.
For every flagged contract, confirm the icon and the prescribed low-performing statement appear on each sampled material that references Star Ratings.
A flagged contract's material referencing Star Ratings without the icon and statement is a reportable failure.
testing.done: the icon obligation is independently re-derived from three years of HPMS ratings and its application is confirmed on every affected material.

testing.step: Trace benefit statements back to the accepted bid
actions: Select ten benefit values per sampled Summary of Benefits and EOC — deductible, maximum out-of-pocket, primary and specialist cost share, a supplemental benefit — and trace each to the accepted Plan Benefit Package.

Confirm every Part A and Part B basic benefit required by 42 CFR 422.101(a),(b) other than hospice is described, and that no description is narrower than the applicable national or local coverage determination.
Compare the printed value to the value configured in the claims and policy administration systems so the member document and the adjudication agree.
Any difference between the document, the bid and the system configuration is an exception with the member population quantified.
testing.done: sampled benefit values agree across the document, the accepted bid and the system configuration, with basic benefit coverage confirmed.

testing.step: Recompute the review period and the first-use date
actions: Read the HPMS submission date and the review route recorded for each sampled material.
Recompute the earliest permitted distribution date by adding the 45-day prior-approval or 5-day File-and-Use period to the submission date.
Compare it to the actual first-use date evidenced by the campaign send log, the print release or the website publication timestamp.
Any use before the recomputed date is a reportable failure, not a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled material's first-use date is on or after its recomputed earliest permitted date, or the breach is reported.

testing.step: Test the ANOC and EOC delivery against September 30
actions: Rebuild the mailing population independently from the policy administration system for enrollees active in the following contract year and reconcile it to the MARx membership file.
Compare the rebuilt population to the mail file sent to the vendor and quantify anyone omitted.
Read the postal and electronic delivery confirmation dates and confirm delivery on or before September 30.
Test that alternate-format and language-preference requests were fulfilled rather than defaulted to standard print.
testing.done: the delivery population reconciles to MARx, delivery is evidenced by September 30, and format and language preferences were honoured.

testing.step: Test the withdrawal of disapproved and superseded materials
actions: For each CMS disapproval in the period, read the stop time recorded and compare it to the disapproval timestamp in HPMS.
Confirm removal from the website, the member portal, the agent portal and every active campaign, and confirm the field recall of printed stock is evidenced.
Confirm the corrected version was resubmitted with a new material ID and that the review period ran again from resubmission.
Confirm the member impact assessment and, where required, the correction notice were completed and logged.
testing.done: every disapproved material was stopped same day, fully withdrawn across channels, correctly resubmitted, and member impact was assessed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the material ID, contract, PBP, what was missing and the member population exposed.
Assign a root cause (model not ingested, benefit content sourced from last year, flag list stale, review period miscomputed, channel not gated, recall incomplete) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any early distribution or missing required disclosure, notify Market Conduct Compliance and Regulatory Counsel the same day for a CMS self-report assessment.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where members were exposed, a same-day self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds for early distribution, missing disclosures and bid inconsistency.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, checked and submitted none of the sampled materials, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee before the Annual Enrollment Period opens and file the workpaper under REG-051-C07.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and pre-AEP committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Policy Admin Ops Lead owns generation and delivery of member notices within the CMS timeframes; the Complaints Manager owns the appeal-related notices and the auto-forward to the Independent Review Entity

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi) (compliance program duty to monitor, audit and respond promptly), 42 CFR 422.137(d) (utilization management committee oversight of the criteria behind denial notices) and 42 CFR 422.101(b) (basic benefits, which sets what may lawfully be denied) read on eCFR, alongside the CMS Parts C and D Enrollee Grievances, Organization/Coverage Determinations and Appeals Guidance and the current OMB-approved notice forms

In-scope processes.value: Generation, timing and delivery of every CMS-required MA member notice: standard and expedited organization determinations, the Integrated or Notice of Denial of Medical Coverage, notice of denial of payment, reconsideration decisions, auto-forward notices to the Independent Review Entity, extension notices, the Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage and the Detailed Explanation of Non-Coverage

In-scope systems.value: Notice triggers raised from the utilization management and claims workflow, letters generated from approved templates and delivered by print vendor and member portal, with every timestamp captured in the case management record

Compliance procedure documented.value: MA Member Notice Timeliness Procedure — request receipt timestamping, clock start rules by request type, template selection, UM criteria and rationale capture, extension rules, delivery channel and proof, auto-forward to the IRE and daily timeliness monitoring

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Operating Officer; re-approved annually and on every CMS guidance update or revision to an OMB-approved notice form, with the UM committee under 42 CFR 422.137(d) approving the criteria language quoted in denial notices

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Standard pre-service organization determination and notice no later than 14 calendar days from receipt of the service request; expedited determination within 72 hours; payment determination within 60 days of receipt; standard reconsideration within 30 days; a 14-day extension only where the enrollee's interest is served and an extension notice is issued; NOMNC delivered at least 2 days before covered services end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case management alerts at 50% and 80% of each clock — day 7 and day 11 of a 14-day determination, hour 36 and hour 58 of a 72-hour expedited case, day 15 and day 24 of a 30-day reconsideration — plus a daily breach-risk queue worked by the supervisor

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Request receipt timestamp, clock calculation, notice PDF as sent, delivery proof, IRE auto-forward confirmation and the UM criteria cited retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every notice issued outside its timeframe, every case auto-forwarded late to the IRE, every notice on a superseded form version and every missing delivery proof is logged with root cause, member impact and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every untimely-notice remediation, every re-issue to affected members and any CMS self-disclosure arising from a pattern of untimeliness

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every organization determination, reconsideration, payment decision and termination-of-services case in the period, by contract and notice type, taken from the case management system and reconciled to the claims denial extract

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of notices within their stated timeframe — 14 calendar days standard, 72 hours expedited, 60 days payment, 30 days reconsideration, NOMNC 2 days before termination; any breach is a fail, and an untimely case not auto-forwarded to the IRE is a reportable failure

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven and continuous; the test runs monthly on the full case population for timeliness and quarterly on a drawn sample for content, mirroring the CMS program audit sampling approach

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside member operations and must not have worked, approved or issued any sampled notice

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly notice timeliness test workpaper (case universe, clock recomputation, delivery proof checks, sampled content review, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C08

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Case universe in the CMS program audit ODAG record layout, plus the notice PDF, delivery proof and clock evidence for any case CMS selects, producible within the days stated in the audit engagement letter

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Officer owns the CMS program audit ODAG response and the Complaints Manager owns state and CMS complaint responses; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a pattern of untimely notices before it is sent

checklist.step: Timestamp every request at the point of receipt
actions: Capture the date and time of every organization determination request at first receipt across all channels — call, fax, provider portal, mail and member portal — including requests arriving out of hours.
Record who made the request (enrollee, appointed representative or prescribing physician) and whether expedited handling was requested or is medically indicated.
Create the case in the case management system with the receipt timestamp copied from the channel record, not typed from memory.
Route misdirected requests to the correct queue the same day without restarting the clock, since the clock runs from first receipt anywhere in the organization.
checklist.done: every request has a channel-sourced receipt timestamp, a requester type, an expedited flag and a case created the same day.

checklist.step: Set the correct clock for the case type
actions: Apply the clock by case type: no later than 14 calendar days from receipt for a standard pre-service organization determination, 72 hours for an expedited determination, 60 days from receipt for a payment determination and 30 days for a standard reconsideration.
Compute and write the due date and time on the case, in the enrollee's time zone where the clock is measured in hours.
Set the system alerts at 50% and 80% of the clock so the case surfaces before it is at risk, not after.
Prevent the clock from being reset by internal reassignment, vendor referral or delegated-entity handoff.
checklist.done: each case shows a computed due date and time by case type, with alerts armed and the clock protected from internal resets.

checklist.step: Screen expedited requests inside the required window
actions: Review every expedited request, and every standard request where a physician indicates that the standard timeframe could seriously jeopardise life, health or ability to regain maximum function.
Grant expedited handling automatically where a physician supports the request, and record the physician's statement on the case.
Where expedited handling is denied, downgrade to the standard 14-day clock, make reasonable efforts to give prompt oral notice and send the required written notice of the downgrade.
Record the screening decision, its time and the clinician who made it.
checklist.done: every expedited request is screened with a recorded decision and time, and every denial of expedition has oral and written notice evidenced.

checklist.step: Capture the clinical rationale and the UM criteria behind an adverse decision
actions: Record the specific benefit provision, coverage rule or utilization management criterion relied on, naming the applicable national or local coverage determination where one exists.
Confirm the criterion used is one the utilization management committee has approved under 42 CFR 422.137(d) and that the current approved version was applied.
Confirm the denied item is not a Part A or Part B basic benefit the plan must cover under 42 CFR 422.101(a),(b), which cannot be denied on plan policy alone.
Write the rationale in plain language the enrollee can act on, and record it in the case for the notice generator to pull.
checklist.done: each adverse decision names an approved UM criterion or coverage rule, is checked against basic benefit coverage, and carries a plain-language rationale.

checklist.step: Generate the notice from the current OMB-approved form
actions: Select the correct form for the case type — the Integrated or Notice of Denial of Medical Coverage for service denials, the notice of denial of payment for payment denials, the reconsideration decision letter, the NOMNC for termination of covered services and the Detailed Explanation of Non-Coverage where the enrollee appeals a termination.
Confirm the template in use is the current OMB-approved version and expiration date, and block generation on any superseded template.
Merge the case fields: enrollee name and member number, the service or claim at issue, the decision, the specific reason, the appeal rights and deadlines, and the plan contact and TTY number.
Produce the notice in the enrollee's recorded language and format preference, with interpreter availability stated.
checklist.done: the notice is generated on the current approved form with a specific reason, appeal rights and the enrollee's language and format honoured.

checklist.step: Apply an extension only where the rules allow it
actions: Grant a 14-day extension on a standard determination only where the enrollee requests it or the plan justifies a need for additional information that is in the enrollee's interest.
Record the specific outstanding information and why obtaining it serves the enrollee, not the plan's workload.
Send the required extension notice stating the reason and the enrollee's right to file an expedited grievance about the delay, within the original timeframe.
Never extend an expedited 72-hour case beyond what the guidance permits, and never extend to cover an internal backlog.
checklist.done: every extension has a recorded enrollee-interest justification and an extension notice issued inside the original timeframe.

checklist.step: Deliver the notice and capture the delivery proof
actions: Send by the channel required for the notice type and the enrollee's election, and give prompt oral notice first where the guidance requires it for expedited cases.
Capture the mail drop date from the print vendor file, or the portal posting timestamp, and attach the as-sent PDF to the case.
For the NOMNC, obtain the enrollee's or representative's signature and date, since delivery must be at least 2 days before covered services end.
Chase undeliverable mail and re-send to a corrected address the same day, logging both attempts.
checklist.done: every notice has an as-sent PDF, a delivery timestamp, and, for the NOMNC, a signed and dated receipt at least 2 days before termination.

checklist.step: Auto-forward untimely and adverse cases to the Independent Review Entity
actions: Identify daily every case where the plan failed to decide within its timeframe and every fully or partially adverse reconsideration.
Forward the case file to the CMS Independent Review Entity within the timeframe the guidance requires, and record the forwarding timestamp and the IRE case number.
Send the enrollee the notice explaining that the case has gone to the IRE and what happens next.
Treat a missed forward as a reportable failure and escalate it to the Head of Compliance the same day.
checklist.done: every untimely or adverse-reconsideration case is forwarded to the IRE with a recorded timestamp and case number, and the enrollee is notified.

checklist.step: Work the daily breach-risk queue
actions: Open the breach-risk queue each morning showing every case past 80% of its clock, sorted by remaining time.
Reassign or escalate each case with a named owner and confirm before end of shift that no case in the queue will breach overnight.
For expedited cases inside their final 12 hours, escalate to the Medical Director on duty by name rather than by queue.
Record the day's queue disposition so the pattern of near-breaches is visible to management.
checklist.done: the breach-risk queue is worked to zero each day with a named owner per case and the disposition recorded.

checklist.step: Monitor delegated entities that issue notices on the plan's behalf
actions: List every delegated medical group, vendor and first-tier or downstream entity authorised to make determinations or issue notices.
Require a monthly case-level file from each with receipt timestamps, decision times, notice dates and delivery proof.
Audit a sample of each delegate's cases against the same clocks the plan applies and report results to the delegation oversight committee.
Issue a corrective action plan where a delegate's timeliness falls below the standard, and revoke delegation where it does not recover.
checklist.done: every delegate submits a monthly case-level file, is sampled against the plan's clocks, and has a corrective action plan where it fails.

checklist.step: Reconcile the notice population to the claims and UM systems
actions: Extract every denied claim and every adverse utilization management decision in the period from the claims and UM systems.
Match each to a notice in the case management system on member, service and date.
Investigate every denial with no matching notice — an adverse decision without a notice is a member-facing failure, not a data gap.
Report the unmatched count and its trend to the Head of Compliance weekly.
checklist.done: every adverse decision in the claims and UM systems matches a generated notice, and unmatched cases are investigated and reported weekly.

checklist.step: Build and validate the CMS program audit universes for notices
actions: Build the organization determination and appeals universes to the record layout in the current CMS Program Audit Protocols, including receipt date, decision date, notification date and disposition.
Run the CMS integrity checks — record counts, mandatory fields, valid code values, date sequencing — and fix defects before submission.
Test that the universe reproduces the same timeliness result as the internal monitoring; a difference means one of the two is wrong.
Refresh the universe monthly so it is audit-ready rather than built under an engagement clock.
checklist.done: the notice universes are built to the current CMS layout, pass integrity checks, reproduce internal timeliness and are refreshed monthly.

checklist.step: Remediate the members affected by an untimely notice
actions: For each breach, determine what the member lost — delayed care, an out-of-pocket payment, a missed appeal window — and quantify it.
Re-open the case where the appeal window was affected, restore the member's rights and communicate the correction in writing.
Where the breach affected a group of members, run a population-level sweep for the same defect rather than fixing only the case that surfaced.
Report the remediation and the member counts to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: each breach has a quantified member impact, a restored appeal right where affected, and a population sweep where the defect was systemic.

checklist.step: Take the timeliness results to the compliance and UM committees
actions: Report monthly timeliness by notice type and contract, the breach count, the IRE auto-forward record and the delegate results.
Take the criteria-related findings to the utilization management committee required by 42 CFR 422.137(d) so the criteria behind repeated denials are reconsidered.
Record the committees' decisions and any corrective action with owners and dates in the GRC platform.
Escalate any sustained pattern of untimeliness to the Head of Compliance for a CMS self-disclosure assessment.
checklist.done: monthly timeliness and criteria findings are minuted at the compliance and UM committees with owned corrective actions.

checklist.step: Archive the notice evidence under the 10-year retention label
actions: File per case the receipt timestamp record, the clock calculation, the as-sent notice PDF, the delivery proof, the NOMNC signature where applicable and the IRE forwarding confirmation under REG-051-C08.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm the record is searchable by member identifier, contract, case type and decision date so a CMS audit sample can be pulled directly.
checklist.done: each case's notice evidence is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by member, contract, case type and date.

testing.step: Build the case universe and reconcile it to the source systems
actions: Extract every organization determination, reconsideration, payment decision and termination-of-services case in the period with receipt, decision and notification timestamps.
Reconcile the extract to the claims denial extract and the utilization management decision log, in both directions.
Add cases handled by delegated entities from their monthly files so delegated volume cannot sit outside the population.
Sign the universe as complete and record the counts by case type in the workpaper.
testing.done: the case universe reconciles to claims, UM and delegate files in both directions and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Recompute the clock for every case in the universe
actions: Recompute elapsed time from the channel-sourced receipt timestamp to the notification timestamp for every case.
Compare each against its own standard — 14 calendar days standard determination, 72 hours expedited, 60 days payment, 30 days reconsideration.
Check no clock was restarted by reassignment, vendor referral or delegate handoff by comparing the first receipt across all channel logs.
Produce a breach list by case type and contract with the overrun in days or hours.
testing.done: every case has an independently recomputed elapsed time against its own standard and a quantified breach list exists.

testing.step: Draw and document the content sample
actions: Take 100% of breaches, 100% of expedited denials and 100% of NOMNC cases where the enrollee appealed.
Draw 30 further cases at random across notice types and contracts using a recorded seed.
Record the universe size, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every case type that failed the prior month as a mandatory retest stratum.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all breaches and expedited denials, and retests prior-month failing case types.

testing.step: Re-perform the notice content review on the as-sent letter
actions: Work from the as-sent PDF and confirm the form is the current OMB-approved version and expiration date, not a superseded template.
Check the notice states the specific reason for the decision in plain language, names the benefit provision or coverage rule relied on, and sets out the appeal rights and deadlines.
Confirm the language and alternate-format preference on the member record was honoured and interpreter availability is stated.
A generic reason such as 'not medically necessary' with no criterion named is a fail.
testing.done: each sampled notice is on a current form, states a specific named reason and appeal rights, and honours language and format preference.

testing.step: Re-perform the coverage judgement behind sampled denials
actions: For each sampled denial, read the utilization management criterion cited and confirm it is the version approved by the UM committee under 42 CFR 422.137(d) at the decision date.
Confirm the denied item was not a Part A or Part B basic benefit the plan must cover under 42 CFR 422.101(a),(b), and check the applicable national or local coverage determination directly.
Reach an independent view on whether the criterion supports the denial, without reading the reviewer's conclusion first.
Any denial of a required basic benefit is a reportable failure escalated the same day.
testing.done: each sampled denial is independently re-judged against the approved criterion and the applicable coverage determination.

testing.step: Verify delivery proof and NOMNC timing
actions: For each sampled case, confirm a mail drop date from the vendor file or a portal posting timestamp exists, not merely a letter generation date.
For expedited cases, confirm prompt oral notice was attempted and recorded before or alongside the written notice.
For NOMNC cases, confirm the signed and dated receipt shows delivery at least 2 days before covered services ended, and recompute the interval.
A generated letter with no delivery evidence counts as undelivered.
testing.done: every sampled notice has delivery evidence, expedited oral notice is recorded, and NOMNC intervals recompute to at least 2 days.

testing.step: Test extensions and the IRE auto-forward
actions: For each extended case, confirm the enrollee requested it or a documented enrollee-interest justification exists, and that the extension notice issued inside the original timeframe.
Reject any extension justified by internal backlog and count it as a breach of the original clock.
For every breach and every adverse reconsideration, confirm the case was forwarded to the Independent Review Entity with a recorded timestamp and IRE case number.
Confirm the enrollee received the notice explaining the IRE referral.
testing.done: extensions are justified in the enrollee's interest and noticed on time, and every breach and adverse reconsideration shows an evidenced IRE forward.

testing.step: Test delegate performance and universe integrity
actions: Sample cases from each delegated entity's monthly file and recompute the clocks on the plan's own standards.
Compare the delegate's reported timeliness to the recomputed result and treat any overstatement as a delegation oversight failure.
Re-run the CMS integrity checks on the organization determination and appeals universes as submitted and confirm they reproduce the internal timeliness result.
Confirm every delegate below standard has an open corrective action plan with a named owner and a due date.
testing.done: delegate timeliness recomputes to their reported figures, universes pass CMS integrity checks and reproduce internal results, and failing delegates have open CAPs.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the case, contract, notice type, the overrun and the member impact.

Assign a root cause (receipt not timestamped at first contact, clock restarted on handoff, expedited screening missed, superseded template, delivery proof not captured, delegate under-reported) and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next monthly cycle and require a member-level remediation where an appeal right was affected.
Where breaches form a pattern by contract or notice type, open a CMS self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the Head of Compliance.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, member remediation where rights were affected, and a self-disclosure assessment on any pattern.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute timeliness rates by notice type against the 100% standard for the 14-day, 72-hour, 60-day and 30-day clocks and the 2-day NOMNC interval.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside member operations and worked no sampled case, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the utilization management committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper under REG-051-C08.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with per-notice-type timeliness rates, a stated conclusion and committee reporting dates is filed in the evidence repository.
